accessibilityConfig.doc: Per-visual screen-reader description. Optional for back-compat: absent reads as `{ description: null }` (follow the title and subtitle) via `migrateAccessibilityConfig`, so no storage version bump.

accessibilityConfig.description.doc: Null = derived from the title and subtitle (`resolveChartDescription`).

annotationsConfig.doc: Per-visual rectangle annotations (shaded regions / highlight boxes overlaid on the plot). Optional for back-compat with visuals saved before annotations existed — falls back to DEFAULT_ANNOTATIONS_CONFIG on load.

annotationsConfig.circles[].backgroundOp.doc: 0..1 fill alpha applied on top of the fill color.

annotationsConfig.circles[].borderOpacit.doc: 0..1 alpha applied to the border stroke.

annotationsConfig.circles[].centerX.doc: Center position. In `"percent"` coordSystem these are 0–1 numbers (plot-area-normalized — x: 0 hugs the y-axis spine, 1 the right edge; y: 0 hugs the BOTTOM spine, 1 the top — the renderer flips to SVG's top-down system).

annotationsConfig.circles[].coordSystem.doc: How `centerX/centerY/radius` are interpreted — see field docs above.

annotationsConfig.circles[].facetKeys.doc: Which facet panels the annotation is drawn on — see `RectangleAnnotation.facetKeys`.

annotationsConfig.circles[].id.doc: Stable id for keying and removal.

annotationsConfig.circles[].name.doc: Optional human label shown in the sidebar list.

annotationsConfig.circles[].radius.doc: Radius magnitude. In `"percent"` mode it's a fraction (0–1) of the `radiusAxis` axis's pixel extent. In `"values"` mode it's a count of data units along `radiusAxis`, projected through that axis's scale — when that axis HAS data units (quantitative / numeric-ordinal).

annotationsConfig.circles[].radiusAxis.doc: Which axis the radius is measured against (its pixel extent in percent mode, its scale in values mode).

annotationsConfig.circles[].radiusUnit.doc: How `radius` is read in `"values"` mode when `radiusAxis` has no data units (see `radius`). Absent = `"percent"`, so a circle toggled from percent to values keeps its size, and circles saved before the field existed render instead of vanishing.

annotationsConfig.circles[].zOrder.doc: "behind" draws under the chart marks; "front" draws above them.

annotationsConfig.images.doc: Pictures placed on the chart. Optional-at-runtime for configs saved before images shipped (the v5→v6 migration backfills `[]`); readers guard with `?? []`.

annotationsConfig.images[].alt.doc: Description for screen readers. Blank = decorative (hidden from the accessibility tree, like the annotation shapes).

annotationsConfig.images[].anchorH.doc: Which point of the picture sits on the anchor.

annotationsConfig.images[].aspect.doc: Natural width / height of the stored picture; sizes the height when the aspect ratio is locked.

annotationsConfig.images[].facetKeys.doc: Which facet panels the annotation is drawn on — see `RectangleAnnotation.facetKeys`.

annotationsConfig.images[].href.doc: The picture as a data URL (PNG / JPEG / SVG…), downscaled at import to `MAX_IMAGE_ANNOTATION_PX`. Blank = no image chosen yet.

annotationsConfig.images[].id.doc: Stable id for keying and removal.

annotationsConfig.images[].name.doc: Optional human label shown in the sidebar list.

annotationsConfig.images[].naturalWidth.doc: Natural width of the stored picture in px (after the import downscale) — what a percent size is a percent OF.

annotationsConfig.images[].width.doc: Rendered width / height, read in `sizeUnit`. With `lockAspect` on the height is DERIVED from the width and `aspect` at render (the stored height is kept in step by the editor); off, both are honored and the picture stretches.

annotationsConfig.images[].x.doc: Anchor x / y — same coordinate rules as `TextAnnotation.x` / `y`.

annotationsConfig.images[].zOrder.doc: "behind" draws under the chart marks; "front" draws above them.

annotationsConfig.lineSegments[].arrowhe.doc: Draw an arrowhead at endpoint B (xMax, yMax). Absent = none.
Multiplier on the head's thickness-derived size; 1 = default.
Which head to draw when `arrowhead` is on.

annotationsConfig.lineSegments[].coordSy.doc: How the endpoints are interpreted — see `RectangleAnnotation`.

annotationsConfig.lineSegments[].facetKe.doc: Which facet panels the annotation is drawn on — see `RectangleAnnotation.facetKeys`.

annotationsConfig.lineSegments[].id.doc: Stable id for keying and removal.

annotationsConfig.lineSegments[].lineCap.doc: Stroke end shape. Absent (lines saved before the option) reads as `DEFAULT_LINE_END_STYLE.lineCap` — the flush end they always had.

annotationsConfig.lineSegments[].lineOpa.doc: 0..1 alpha applied to the line stroke.

annotationsConfig.lineSegments[].name.doc: Optional human label shown in the sidebar list.

annotationsConfig.lineSegments[].xMin.doc: Endpoint A x / endpoint B x. Same number-vs-string + percent/values rules as the rectangle's `xMin/xMax` — see `RectangleAnnotation`.

annotationsConfig.lineSegments[].yMin.doc: Endpoint A y / endpoint B y. Same rules as the rectangle's `yMin/yMax` (percent y=0 hugs the BOTTOM spine; the renderer flips to SVG top-down).

annotationsConfig.lineSegments[].zOrder.doc: "behind" draws the line UNDER the chart marks; "front" draws ABOVE them (the usual choice for a reference / trend line).

annotationsConfig.rectangles[].backgroun.doc: 0..1 fill alpha applied on top of the fill color.

annotationsConfig.rectangles[].borderDas.doc: User-typed custom SVG dasharray (e.g. `"2,2"`). When set it WINS over `borderDash` — the picker's Custom choice. Null/absent = use `borderDash` (also the shape of annotations saved before Custom existed). Parsed via `sanitizeCustomDasharray` at render time.

annotationsConfig.rectangles[].borderOpa.doc: 0..1 alpha applied to the border stroke.

annotationsConfig.rectangles[].coordSyst.doc: How `xMin/xMax/yMin/yMax` are interpreted: - `"percent"` (default): plot-area-normalized (0–1), same as the original behavior. Useful for "always anchor to the bottom-left quadrant" annotations regardless of data. - `"values"`: data values along each axis.

annotationsConfig.rectangles[].facetKeys.doc: Which facet panels the annotation is drawn on, when the chart is faceted. `null`/`undefined` (the default) means "all facets" — the legacy behavior, so saved annotations keep showing everywhere.

annotationsConfig.rectangles[].id.doc: Stable id for keying and removal.

annotationsConfig.rectangles[].name.doc: Optional human label shown in the sidebar list.

annotationsConfig.rectangles[].text.doc: Optional text label drawn INSIDE the rectangle. Empty/absent = no text. The text block is centered vertically within the box; horizontal placement follows `textAlign`, inset from the box edge by `textPadding`. A literal `\n` in the string forces a line break.

annotationsConfig.rectangles[].textItali.doc: Italic / underlined label text. Absent = off (pre-Style-row saves).

annotationsConfig.rectangles[].textPaddi.doc: Inner padding between the rectangle edge and the text, in px.

annotationsConfig.rectangles[].xMin.doc: Horizontal extent. In `"percent"` coordSystem these are 0–1 numbers (plot-area-normalized — xMin=0 hugs the y-axis spine, xMax=1 hugs the right edge).

annotationsConfig.rectangles[].yMin.doc: Vertical extent. Same number-vs-string rules as `xMin/xMax`. In `"percent"` coordSystem yMin=0 hugs the BOTTOM spine (cartesian convention) and yMax=1 hugs the top; the renderer flips to SVG's top-down coordinate system.

annotationsConfig.rectangles[].zOrder.doc: "behind" draws the rectangle UNDER the chart marks (e.g. a shaded background band); "front" draws ABOVE marks (e.g. a callout box highlighting a region).

annotationsConfig.texts[].backgroundOpac.doc: 0..1 fill alpha applied on top of the fill color.

annotationsConfig.texts[].borderOpacity.doc: 0..1 alpha applied to the border stroke.

annotationsConfig.texts[].coordSystem.doc: How `x`/`y` are interpreted — see the field docs above.

annotationsConfig.texts[].cornerRadius.doc: Rounded-corner radius for the background box, in px. 0 = square.

annotationsConfig.texts[].facetKeys.doc: Which facet panels the annotation is drawn on — see `RectangleAnnotation.facetKeys`.

annotationsConfig.texts[].id.doc: Stable id for keying and removal.

annotationsConfig.texts[].name.doc: Optional human label shown in the sidebar list.

annotationsConfig.texts[].text.doc: The label itself. A literal `\n` forces a line break.

annotationsConfig.texts[].textAlign.doc: Line alignment AND the horizontal anchor edge — see the type doc.

annotationsConfig.texts[].textItalic.doc: Italic / underlined label text. Absent = off (pre-Style-row saves).

annotationsConfig.texts[].textPadding.doc: Inner padding between the text and the background box edge, in px. Also what the box grows by, since it's sized to the text.

annotationsConfig.texts[].x.doc: Anchor x. In `"percent"` coordSystem a 0–1 plot-area-normalized number (0 hugs the y-axis spine, 1 the right edge). In `"values"` a raw axis value — number for quantitative/numeric-ordinal (epoch ms for temporal), string for categorical — fed through the chart's x position scale.

annotationsConfig.texts[].y.doc: Anchor y. Same rules as `x`; in `"percent"` mode 0 hugs the BOTTOM spine (cartesian convention) and 1 the top; in `"pixels"` whole px UP from the plot's TOP edge (negative = inside the plot); in the bottom-corner pixel systems whole px UP from the BOTTOM edge (negative = below the plot).

annotationsConfig.texts[].zOrder.doc: "behind" draws under the chart marks; "front" draws above them.

captionConfig.doc: Per-visual caption — a free-floating text box rendered below the x-axis title. Optional for back-compat with visuals saved before captions existed; falls back to DEFAULT_CAPTION_CONFIG on load.

captionConfig.backgroundColor.doc: Background fill. `backgroundOpacity: 0` = transparent (no visible box); there's no separate on/off toggle — opacity 0 IS "off".

captionConfig.borderEnabled.doc: Border. Gated by `borderEnabled` (an explicit toggle, mirroring the Legend panel's "Border box") so the box can carry a stored width/color without drawing until the user opts in.

captionConfig.enabled.doc: Master switch. Even when true, an empty `text` renders nothing.

captionConfig.height.doc: Box height. `0` = auto (grows to fit the wrapped text).

captionConfig.italic.doc: Italic caption text. Optional: absent = upright (what every caption saved before the Style row drew), so no migration.

captionConfig.offsetX.doc: Horizontal nudge from the default (centered) position. `+` moves right.

captionConfig.offsetY.doc: Vertical nudge from the default (below x-axis title) position. `+` moves down.

captionConfig.padding.doc: Inner padding between the box edge and the text, in px.

captionConfig.text.doc: Caption body. Long text wraps to the box width; literal `\n` forces a break.

captionConfig.underline.doc: Underlined caption text. Optional: absent = no underline.

captionConfig.width.doc: Box width. `0` = auto (spans the full canvas width).

channelConfigs.angle.customFormat.doc: d3-format string for tick labels (quantitative) or d3-time-format string (temporal). Empty / undefined → use the scale's default formatter.

channelConfigs.angle.donutHoleRadius.doc: Pie-mode donut hole, as a percentage (0–90) of the pie's outer radius. `0` renders a solid pie; any positive value renders a donut whose center hole is that fraction of the radius. Only consulted by PiePlot (pies / pies-x / pies-y); radar ignores it.

channelConfigs.angle.spine.doc: Spoke color + thickness — the lines from center to perimeter at each angle tick. Defaults to the system theme's spine color when unset.

channelConfigs.angle.spine.opacity.doc: Stroke opacity [0,1]. Only the radar spoke spine reads this (the R position menu's Spine section); cartesian axis spines leave it unset. Sparse: absent = 1.

channelConfigs.angle.tickCount.doc: Number of evenly-spaced spokes for quantitative / temporal angle. Ignored for categorical / ordinal — those always get one spoke per domain value.

channelConfigs.angle.tickLabelAngle.doc: Rotation (degrees) applied to perimeter tick labels around their anchor. 0 keeps them upright (matches the chosen "Stay horizontal" default).

channelConfigs.angle.tickLabelDistance.doc: Extra radial distance (px) between the spoke tip and the perimeter label, on top of the renderer's base gap. Positive pushes labels away from the chart; negative pulls them onto it. 0 = base gap.

channelConfigs.angle.tickLabelEvery.doc: Label every Nth spoke (1 = label all). Spokes still draw at every angle tick; only the perimeter labels thin out — the radar analog of the categorical axis's "Label every" stride.

channelConfigs.area.overrides.doc: Per-category radius overrides for a NON-numeric ordinal field mapped to area, keyed by the category's string form. An unset category uses the even min→max spread, so the auto-spread stays the zero-config default and each category is individually pinnable.

channelConfigs.area.sizeBy.doc: How the mapped value translates to circle size: - "area" (default, absent): the value drives the circle's AREA — radius grows with √value. Honest proportions (a doubled value doubles the ink), and the only mode where packed-circle containers read as the sum of their children.

channelConfigs.aspectRatio.doc: Aesthetics → Aspect ratio (see AspectRatioConfig). Absent = off.

channelConfigs.axesBehindMarks.doc: Aesthetics → Draw order → "Draw axes behind marks". Default (absent / false): gridlines paint under the marks and the spine + ticks + tick labels + axis title paint OVER them, so a bar or point crossing the axis never hides it.

channelConfigs.backgroundColor.doc: Per-visual chart background color. `null` (or absent) means transparent — host page / iframe shows through.

channelConfigs.brightness.min.doc: Anchored levels like `SaturationConfig`: 0.5 leaves the base color's lightness alone, 0 is black, 1 is white.

channelConfigs.brightnessSlots.areaPoint.doc: Anchored levels, NOT absolute HSL components: 0.5 leaves the base color's saturation alone, 0 is fully gray, 1 fully saturated. See `anchoredComponent` in lib/scales.

channelConfigs.canvasSize.margins.doc: White space between the canvas edge and the nearest PAINTED content on each side (px). Sparse: an absent side is "auto" — whatever slack the layout leaves today.

channelConfigs.canvasSize.unit.doc: Unit the sidebar's width/height inputs display in. Display-only — width/height above stay px-truth (converted at 96 px/inch, matching the Export modal's unit convention). Absent = px.

channelConfigs.categoricalPalettePattern.doc: Per-color pattern-ink override paired with `categoricalPalette`. Same length when present; entries may be `null` to fall back to the global `patternInkColor`. Resolved from the source `SavedCategoricalPalette` at theme-snapshot time.

channelConfigs.colorSlots.doc: Generic color targets beyond fill (`hue`) and outline (`outlineHue`): line, rug, violin/box stroke + fill, lollipop stem, radar spine. Each is an independent optional color encoding surfaced as a subheader in the Color menu.

channelConfigs.colorSlots.areaPointFill..doc: Conditional color rules (the Color menu's "+ Add color rule" rows; the Line slot is the one that surfaces them). An implicit rule (`> 0`) tests the slot's mapped variable's value; a `{Variable}` rule tests that variable in the mark's rows.

channelConfigs.connection.axisStem.doc: Scatter-only: draw a stem from each point to an axis (lollipop charts). Unlike the group polyline above, this is a PER-POINT derived mark — it needs no connection field and ignores grouping. - `"none"` (default): no stems.

channelConfigs.connection.axisStemCustom.doc: The data-space threshold the `"custom-x"` / `"custom-y"` stems land on. `null` / absent reads as 0. Optional so visuals saved before the custom options existed load unchanged.

channelConfigs.connection.chordAxis.doc: Chord layout only: the circular value axis around the ring. Absent / `enabled: false` draws no axis (the historical look). Optional so visuals saved before it existed load unchanged.

channelConfigs.connection.chordAxis.cust.doc: d3-format spec for tick labels; `""` = auto (SI-prefixed from the step, e.g. "5k"). Same semantics as `AxisConfig.customFormat`.

channelConfigs.connection.chordAxis.labe.doc: Label every Nth tick mark (1 = label all). Labeling every tick gets crowded at the auto step, so the default labels every 5th — the d3 chord convention.

channelConfigs.connection.chordAxis.spin.doc: The "spine" here is the thin arc drawn along each group's outer edge (the circular analogue of the x / y axis line); absent = `DEFAULT_SPINE_CONFIG`.
Stroke opacity [0,1]. Only the radar spoke spine reads this (the R position menu's Spine section); cartesian axis spines leave it unset. Sparse: absent = 1.

channelConfigs.connection.chordAxis.tick.doc: Target number of tick marks around the FULL ring — the axis is continuous (flow values), so it takes a count like the continuous x / y axes, not a categorical "tick every" stride.
Tick LABEL font override; unset fields inherit the base text font (`labels.baseFont.text`), exactly like the x / y tick-label fonts.

channelConfigs.connection.chordAxis.vert.doc: "Make all tick labels vertical": draw every tick label upright in screen space (unrotated, reading left-to-right) just outside its tick, instead of the default radial orientation (text runs outward along the tick, flipping past 6 o'clock). Sparse — absent / `false` = radial.

channelConfigs.connection.customDashPatt.doc: User-typed custom dasharray for the default line dash (the Pattern panel's no-field "Custom" pick). When it parses to a valid dasharray (see `sanitizeCustomDasharray`) it wins over `defaultDashPattern`; per-group `dashPatterns` overrides still win over both.

channelConfigs.connection.dashAlternateC.doc: Per-line alternating colors for non-solid patterns. The "alternate" is the color shown in the gap between dashes; setting it makes a dashed line read as two-color (e.g. dark green dashes on light green background).

channelConfigs.connection.dashGapColor.doc: Single dash-gap color override for charts with NO hue encoding (one line color → one gap swatch in the panel). With hue mapped, per-category overrides live in `dashAlternateColors` keyed by hue value instead. `null` / absent = no override (palette-paired chain applies).

channelConfigs.connection.dashGapFill.doc: Whether the gaps between dashes are painted (an underlay polyline in the alternate color) so a dashed line reads as one connected two-color line, or left empty so the line is truly dashed.

channelConfigs.connection.dashPatterns.doc: Per-line dash pattern overrides keyed by line group value (the connection field's value, or the hue value in area mode). When a key is missing the line falls back to `defaultDashPattern`.

channelConfigs.connection.dashRange.doc: "Apply pattern to range": every line's dash (per-category or the global default) draws only within [min, max] along the axis the line runs along; outside renders solid. One GLOBAL window (a forecast boundary is one date for every series).

channelConfigs.connection.defaultDashPat.doc: Default dash pattern applied to every line that doesn't have a per-group override. Applies in scatter+connection AND area-line modes.

channelConfigs.connection.fill.doc: In areas mode only: `"area"` fills the region below each layer down to the baseline (or the layer below it when stacked); `"line"` renders just the top edge as a polyline (line chart). Ignored in scatter mode, where connection always renders as polylines.

channelConfigs.connection.fillPolygon.doc: Radar-mode only: when true, the closed polygon connecting each series' points fills with its hue color, at the series' opacity times the Opacity panel's "Polygon fill" slot (`opacitySlots .polygonFill`). When false, only the polygon outline draws.

channelConfigs.connection.flowTargetFiel.doc: Flow layouts (chord / sankey) only: the dataset column holding each edge's TARGET node (`Stop` when connection maps `Start`). The connection field is the SOURCE; each row is a directed edge source → target weighted by the `area` field.

channelConfigs.connection.hierarchyIdFie.doc: Packed-circles only: the dataset column holding each row's own node IDENTITY (e.g. `Child` when connection maps `Parent`).

channelConfigs.connection.hierarchyLayou.doc: Which layout renders the hierarchy (packed circles is the default). All five layouts — three trees (pack / treemap / sunburst) and two flows (chord / sankey) — share ONE encoding signature (`area` + optional `connection`, no positions), so encodings alone can't distinguish them — this config gates m…

channelConfigs.connection.lineCap.doc: Cap style for OPEN line ends — scatter connection polylines and area/line-mode layer edges (dash segments too). Radar polygons are closed, so caps never show there.

channelConfigs.connection.lineCapTickLen.doc: Length of the `"tick"` cap's perpendicular mark, in px. `null` / absent = AUTO, derived from the line's thickness (`autoLineEndTickLength`). Only read when `lineCap` is `"tick"`.

channelConfigs.connection.linePalette.doc: Resolved colors for `linePaletteId`. Mirrors the way `configs.categoricalPalette` shadows `categoricalPaletteId` so renderers don't have to re-resolve from the theme on every paint.

channelConfigs.connection.linePaletteId.doc: Optional categorical-palette ID for line strokes in area mode. Lets the user pick a separate palette for the area-layer outlines while the fill keeps its own palette (`configs.categoricalPaletteId`). When `null` / omitted, lines inherit each layer's fill color (the default — what most charts want).

channelConfigs.connection.pointEveryN.doc: Stride for `pointSampling: "every-n"`. Ignored otherwise. Clamped to >= 1 by the renderer.

channelConfigs.connection.pointIndices.doc: 1-based point positions for `pointSampling: "custom"` (the user's "Custom Nth point" list, typed comma-separated). Stored STRUCTURED as numbers, never as the typed string. Ignored in every other mode. Optional for back-compat with visuals saved before it existed — absent reads as empty.

channelConfigs.connection.pointSampling.doc: Per-line point sampling. Lines themselves always use every data point (so the polyline still passes through everything); these options only control which dots / shapes get drawn AT each point. - `"all"` (default): every point gets a marker — current behavior.

channelConfigs.connection.smoothing.doc: Line smoothing amount in [0, 1] for scatter connection lines and area/line-mode layer edges. 0 (the default) draws straight segments through the points; higher values round the corners via a cardinal spline (see `lib/linePath.buildLinePath`). Radar polygons ignore this.

channelConfigs.connection.strokeColor.doc: In area / line mode only: global stroke color for layer top edges (separators in area mode, the polyline itself in line mode). `null` means "inherit from each layer's hue color" — the default, which gives every layer a visible stroke matching its fill.

channelConfigs.connection.thickness.doc: Line thickness in pixels — the single value applied to every line, and the per-category fallback when `thicknessByValue` has no entry for a group.

channelConfigs.connection.thicknessByVal.doc: Per-line thickness overrides (px), keyed by the stringified value of `thicknessField` when set, else by the connection field's value (the hue value in area mode, matching `dashPatterns`).

channelConfigs.connection.thicknessField.doc: "Vary by" variable for per-line thickness. When set, each line's thickness is looked up in `thicknessByValue` by its representative row's value for this field (the same first-row convention the line color slot uses), so thickness can follow any categorical variable that is constant within a line — n…

channelConfigs.defaultPatternInk.doc: Ink for `defaultPattern`. `null` (the default) = the palette-paired ink for the color under the tile (the mark's fill, or the Pattern panel's Background override), else the theme's `patternInkColor`; a hex is an explicit pick. See `resolveDefaultPatternInk`.

channelConfigs.drawOrder.doc: Paint (z-) order for overlapping point marks — scatter, dot map, bubble map. `null`/absent = the renderer's default: dataset row order for scatter (later rows draw on top), largest-circle-first for the geo maps (small bubbles stay visible).

channelConfigs.facet.colAxisOverrides.doc: Mirror of `rowAxisOverrides` for the x-axis per column.

channelConfigs.facet.gapX.doc: Horizontal whitespace between panel plot rectangles, in pixels. Measured plot-edge to plot-edge: 0 = neighbouring plots touch, negative values overlap them (ridgeline use case).

channelConfigs.facet.gapY.doc: Vertical whitespace between panel plot rectangles, in pixels. Same semantics as gapX. Facet labels for the row below render in this whitespace, so this should typically be >= the facet label height (~20px) to avoid the labels overlapping the row above's plot.

channelConfigs.facet.gapsFrom.doc: Marks gapX / gapY as plot-edge-to-plot-edge. Before 2026-10-20 they were measured between whole cells (plot + axis chrome), so 0 still left the chrome between plots; `measureFacetGapsFromPlotEdges` (storage/migrations.ts) shifts an unmarked config onto the new measure once and stamps this, which kee…

channelConfigs.facet.gridPanelAxisOverri.doc: Grid mode's per-panel axis range overrides, keyed by the panel's ROW facet value and then its COLUMN value — two user values kept as two keys, never joined. The unmapped side of a row-only / col-only grid keys as `FACET_PANEL_ALL`.
"Custom breaks" for this panel's x / y axis — see `AxisRangeOverride.ticks`.

channelConfigs.facet.hideEmptyPanels.doc: Grid mode (both facetRow AND facetCol mapped): drop cross-product cells with no data and compact the survivors. Layout adapts to how evenly the surviving panels distribute — see resolveFacetPanels' compactNonEmptyGrid.

channelConfigs.facet.overallRRange.doc: R-axis range overrides for polar (radar) charts. Mirrors the cartesian `overallYRange` / `rowAxisOverrides` / etc. family but kept on dedicated fields so switching between cartesian and polar modes doesn't cross-pollute settings.

channelConfigs.facet.overallYRange.doc: Overall y-axis range applied when `shareY === "all"` and y is quantitative or temporal. Lets the user pin the shared axis to a "pretty" start (e.g. 0) or an upper bound even though d3-nice would otherwise pick something larger. Either bound may be omitted to keep auto-fit on that side.

channelConfigs.facet.panelAxisOverrides.doc: Wrap mode's per-panel axis range overrides, keyed by the facet value (stringified). Only consulted when neither share-axis flag is on for that axis.

channelConfigs.facet.panelAxisOverrides..doc: "Custom breaks" for this panel's x / y axis — see `AxisRangeOverride.ticks`.

channelConfigs.facet.panelOrder.doc: Per-panel display order keyed by facet value (stringified). Values with an entry sort ascending by the number; values without fall through in their natural (data-encounter) order.

channelConfigs.facet.panelWidth.doc: Optional pixel-precise inner-width override for EVERY panel. When set (positive number), the solver bypasses the proportional / equal-split distribution and sizes every panel's `inner.width` to this value.

channelConfigs.facet.proportionalPanelSi.doc: "Size panels by unit" for polar charts — scales each panel's rendered radius proportionally to its R range (radar) or its total slice value (pie). Off = every panel has the same diameter; on = panels with bigger underlying values render bigger. Has no effect outside polar modes.

channelConfigs.facet.proportionalSizing.doc: Size each panel proportional to its number of categories on the non-measure axis. Only meaningful when that axis isn't shared — with a shared axis every panel sees the same domain so equal sizing is already the right answer. Defaults to `true`.

channelConfigs.facet.proportionalSizingB.doc: Same idea as `proportionalSizing`, but the weight is each panel's data range on its quantitative axis instead of its category count.

channelConfigs.facet.proportionalSizingX.doc: Per-axis sizing modes. Drives panel widths (X) and heights (Y) when proportional sizing is on. Migrated from the older global flags `proportionalSizing` / `proportionalSizingByUnit`.

channelConfigs.facet.rowAxisOverrides.doc: Per-row y-axis range overrides. Keyed by the row's facet value (stringified). Only consulted when `shareY === "perGroup"` AND the y-axis variable is continuous (quantitative or temporal); the UI for these overrides is hidden otherwise.

channelConfigs.facet.shareR.doc: Polar-chart (radar / pie) share modes. Polar plots aren't cartesian — the R axis and the angle axis don't have a natural row vs col bias, so they each get a 4-way picker: "none" = every panel its own scale "perRow" = panels in the same layout row share "perCol" = panels in the same layout column sha…

channelConfigs.facet.shareX.doc: Tri-state scale sharing for the x-axis. "all" = one shared x-axis across the grid; "perGroup" = one per column (each column's panels share x); "none" = every panel its own x. Legacy boolean values (true / false) and `undefined` are normalized via migrateShareValue, so saved visuals continue to load.

channelConfigs.facet.shareY.doc: Same as shareX for the y-axis: "all" = one shared y; "perGroup" = one per row; "none" = every panel its own y.

channelConfigs.fillColorRules.doc: Conditional FILL color rules (Color → Fill → "+ Add color rule"). An implicit rule (`> 0`) tests the Color variable's value for the mark; a `{Variable}` rule tests that variable in the mark's rows — the only form that can fire while no Color variable is mapped.

channelConfigs.hexbin.doc: Hexbin binning (not a channel — chart-level, but configured from the Color panel since the hue mapping is what enables hexbin mode).

channelConfigs.hexbin.binCount.doc: Target hexagon columns across the x domain. Unset reads as the default (20, `DEFAULT_HEXBIN_BIN_COUNT` in hexbins.ts).

channelConfigs.hue.customStops.doc: N-stop user-defined custom gradient — read only when palette is `"custom"`. The first/last stops anchor the gradient; any number of additional middle stops are allowed. The legacy `lowColor`/`midColor`/`highColor` fields stay for backwards compatibility with saved charts that pre-date this field.

Read only by the custom-gradient paths (customLinear / customDiverging / manual stops); presets are fully-specified ramps with nothing left to blend.

channelConfigs.hue.sourcePaletteId.doc: Records the dropdown selection that originated this config — a preset name (`"viridis"`), a saved gradient ID, `"custom"`, etc. Survives color edits so a "Reset colors" action can re-resolve to the originating palette's defaults instead of switching the whole palette type.

channelConfigs.hueCategoricalStash.doc: Mirror stash for the categorical `hue` config, saved when a quantitative field replaces it — per-value color overrides survive a round-trip through a gradient the same way.

channelConfigs.hueQuantStash.doc: Stash of the last quantitative `hue` config, saved when the hue encoding switches to a categorical/derived source (the live quant config is dropped then so the renderer can't confuse the two kinds).

channelConfigs.hueQuantStash.customStops.doc: N-stop user-defined custom gradient — read only when palette is `"custom"`. channelConfigs.length.barGapPx.doc: Bar charts: fixed gap between bars in PIXELS — bar width is whatever remains of each category slot, so one knob controls both. BarPlot converts it to the band-padding fraction per panel, which keeps the pixel gap uniform across facet panels of different widths.

channelConfigs.length.render.doc: What a mapped Length draws when BOTH position channels are mapped too (`x + y + length`). `"segments"` (absent / default) keeps the line-segment scatter — each point is a segment whose length is the variable.

channelConfigs.length.segmentLineCap.doc: Segment end caps. "square" ends flush at the endpoints (SVG butt), matching Connection's Line cap. Absent = "round".

channelConfigs.length.segmentThickness.doc: Scatter line segments (Length / default length): stroke width in px. Absent = `DEFAULT_SEGMENT_THICKNESS`; 0 hides the segments.

channelConfigs.length.segmentThicknessBy.doc: Per-level segment thickness, keyed by `String(row[field])`. Seeded with every level when a Vary-by field is picked.

channelConfigs.length.segmentThicknessFi.doc: "Vary by" variable for per-level segment thickness. null/absent = single level. Keyed with `segmentThicknessByValue`; a field that no longer exists renders as single level.

channelConfigs.opacitySlots.doc: Per-part opacity targets (border + the same set of slots as color, minus fill which reuses the overall `opacity` encoding). Each is an independent optional opacity encoding surfaced as a subheader in the Opacity menu. Sparse — an absent slot means the part renders at its registry `defaultLevel`.

channelConfigs.ordinalPaletteId.doc: Ordinal palette settings. Used when the hue field's effective type is `ordinal`. Mirrors the categorical fields but pulled from the theme's `ordinalPalettes` list so themes can supply sequential (light → dark) palettes that read as ordered.

channelConfigs.outlineCategoricalPalette.doc: Outline-color palette selection for the `outlineHue` channel, kept independent of the fill-hue palette (`categoricalPalette` / `ordinalPalette`) so picking an outline palette never disturbs the fill.

channelConfigs.outlineHue.doc: Color scale that drives mark *outline* (stroke) color, mapped to its own field via the `outlineHue` encoding. Reuses the `HueConfig` shape (categorical palette or quantitative gradient). Independent of `hue`, which drives fill.

channelConfigs.outlineHue.customStops.doc: N-stop user-defined custom gradient — read only when palette is `"custom"`. The first/last stops anchor the gradient; any number of additional middle stops are allowed. The legacy `lowColor`/`midColor`/`highColor` fields stay for backwards compatibility with saved charts that pre-date this field.

Read only by the custom-gradient paths (customLinear / customDiverging / manual stops); presets are fully-specified ramps with nothing left to blend.

channelConfigs.panelBorder.doc: Aesthetics → Chart background → panel border (see PanelBorderConfig). Absent = off.

channelConfigs.pattern.areaPointOverride.doc: AREA-CHART POINT FILL — the point markers on an area chart's layer lines take their own pattern pick, separate from the area body (which reads the base `overrides` / `inkColors` / `defaultPattern`, as the marks' fill always has).

channelConfigs.pattern.backgroundColor.doc: The tile color under a pattern when hue does NOT drive the mark's fill. `null` (the default) = the mark's own fill, so a patterned bar keeps its color and the pattern ink pairs with that color through the palette; a hex is an explicit override.

channelConfigs.pattern.customDashOverrid.doc: Per-category user-typed SVG dasharray string (e.g., "2,2", "2,4,5,2"). Wins over `dashOverrides` for that category. Lives separately so the built-in palette index in `dashOverrides` doesn't need a wider type. Empty string clears the override.

channelConfigs.pattern.customPatterns.doc: Per-chart custom fill patterns (uploaded black-and-white images: an SVG kept as vector, a PNG / JPEG reduced to a grayscale ink mask — see `lib/customPatterns`).

channelConfigs.pattern.dashOverrides.doc: Per-category line-dash index (into DASH_CYCLE), or "none" for a solid line. Only consulted by `renderConnectionLines` in line chart context. When unset for a category, the line auto-cycles through DASH_CYCLE by the category's position in its pattern field's unique-values list.

channelConfigs.pattern.defaultPolygonPat.doc: No-variable default polygon pattern (palette index); null/absent = none. The analogue of `ChannelConfigs.defaultPattern` for polygons.
Ink for `defaultPolygonPattern`; null/absent = the theme's pattern ink (`ChannelConfigs.defaultPatternInk`).

channelConfigs.pattern.defaultRotation.doc: Rotation for the no-variable default pattern (`ChannelConfigs.defaultPattern`); null/absent = 0°.

channelConfigs.pattern.defaultScale.doc: Scale for the no-variable default pattern (`ChannelConfigs.defaultPattern`); null/absent = ×1.

channelConfigs.pattern.inkColors.doc: Per-category ink color (hex). Missing categories fall back to DEFAULT_PATTERN_INK.

channelConfigs.pattern.overrides.doc: Per-category palette index (which of the 6 palette shapes this category's pattern uses), or "none" to render the category with no pattern overlay (just the underlying hue / background color). Governs POINT FILL patterns (SVG fills on marks).

channelConfigs.pattern.pointOutlineDash.doc: POINT OUTLINE DASH (polygon mode / radar): the dash the point glyphs' outline ring draws with — the Pattern menu's "Point outline" subsection, the fourth radar target beside Point fill, Connection line and Polygon fill.

channelConfigs.pattern.polygonInkColors.doc: Per pattern-category ink for the polygon pattern (hex). Missing categories fall back to the hue-paired ink, then DEFAULT_PATTERN_INK.

channelConfigs.pattern.polygonOverrides.doc: RADAR POLYGON FILL — a pattern pick SEPARATE from the point fill, read only while `connection.fillPolygon` is on. The Pattern menu's "Polygon fill" subsection writes these four fields; the mark points keep reading `overrides` / `inkColors` / `defaultPattern`.

channelConfigs.pattern.rotations.doc: PATTERN ROTATION — the angle (degrees, clockwise) the pattern tile grid is turned by, per point-fill category: 45° lays the diagonal stripes horizontal, −45° stands them vertical.

channelConfigs.pattern.scales.doc: PATTERN SCALE — zoom on the pattern tile, per point-fill category (×1 = the palette's native tile; ×2 draws the dots / stripes twice as big and twice as far apart).

channelConfigs.pattern.segmentPattern.doc: How Pattern paints a scatter LINE SEGMENT (Length / Angle marks). `"fill"` strokes the segment with the pattern tile, as a bar would be filled; `"dash"` makes Pattern the segment's dash style (the same dash cycle / per-category dash picks a connection line uses).

channelConfigs.pattern.stackMode.doc: Stack/group/overlay layout when pattern is the highest-precedence mapped color channel (hue > pattern > brightness > opacity > saturation). Read by `resolveStackMode`; the Pattern panel exposes the toggle only when it owns layout.

channelConfigs.pattern.violinField.doc: What the violin / box body's pattern VARIES BY — the subsection's "Vary by", the analogue of a color slot's field. Absent = Auto: the Pattern variable, as for the points (per-level picks in `violinOverrides` keyed by its levels, none mapped = the default pattern).

channelConfigs.pattern.violinOverrides.doc: VIOLIN / BOX FILL — the distribution overlay's body (what the Color panel's "Violin / box fill" slot colors) takes its own pattern pick, separate from the point fill, the way the radar polygon does. Read only while a violin or box overlay is on (`overlayOn`).

channelConfigs.r.breaks.doc: Extra pinned tick positions for a continuous axis, ADDED to the auto `tickCount` layout (set `tickCount: 0` and list breaks for fully custom ticks). Tick labels follow the ticks — every tick gets a label. Empty / absent = auto only. Numbers are axis values (epoch ms for temporal).

channelConfigs.r.categoricalTickStride.doc: Stride between visible ticks on a categorical/ordinal axis. `1` (the default) shows every category. `2` shows every other, `3` every third, etc. — useful when there are too many categories to label each one cleanly. The first and last categories always render so the axis ends stay anchored.

channelConfigs.r.customFormat.doc: d3-format (quantitative) or d3-time-format (temporal) string. Empty string means "use the scale's default formatter". The sidebar exposes a dropdown of presets that populate this field; the user can refine the resulting spec by hand.

channelConfigs.r.distributionOverlay.doc: Distribution overlays — meaningful only when this axis is quantitative and the other axis is categorical.

channelConfigs.r.distributionOverlay.box.doc: Multiplier on the box's thickness — the fat dimension perpendicular to the value axis (horizontal for a vertical box, vertical for a horizontal one). 1 = the default (a box spanning ~36% of the category band); larger makes the box fatter/taller, smaller makes it skinnier.

channelConfigs.r.distributionOverlay.col.doc: Stroke color used when hue isn't mapped (so there's no per-category palette to inherit from) and no per-category override exists.
Per-category stroke overrides keyed by stringified category value. Wins over hue inheritance and the default `color`.

channelConfigs.r.distributionOverlay.fil.doc: Fill color (with reduced opacity) under the same conditions.
Per-category fill overrides. Same precedence as `colorOverrides` for fills.

channelConfigs.r.distributionOverlay.mar.doc: Box plot only, and only while `showPoints` is false: draw one point per box at the category's arithmetic mean.

channelConfigs.r.distributionOverlay.sho.doc: Render a Tukey box (q1/median/q3 + 1.5*IQR whiskers + outliers) per category.

Render a standalone density curve — a single KDE line rising from the axis baseline (not mirrored like a violin). Only meaningful in the single-quantitative-variable case (the same situation a histogram applies), so it's surfaced as a sibling of Histogram in the Distribution control.
Render a mirrored KDE polygon per category.
When false, the underlying scatter marks are hidden so the overlay stands alone (classic violin-only / box-only plot). Defaults to true so enabling an overlay on a strip plot keeps the dots visible.

channelConfigs.r.gridlines.breaks.doc: User-pinned gridline positions on a continuous axis — the gridline counterpart of `AxisConfig.breaks`. Plain axis values (epoch-ms for temporal). When non-empty these win over `count` entirely. Optional so visuals saved before it existed load unchanged.

channelConfigs.r.gridlines.count.doc: Gridline count. `null` means "match the axis tick count" (one gridline per labeled tick) — this is the default and what users most often want. Set to a specific number to decouple from ticks.

channelConfigs.r.histogram.doc: Histogram binning for a quantitative category axis in bar charts. Absent / `enabled: false` means "no binning" (the default). Optional so existing saved configs load unchanged — a missing value reads as disabled.

channelConfigs.r.histogram.binCount.doc: Number of equal-width bins. Clamped to >= 1 at render time.

channelConfigs.r.histogram.densityBandwi.doc: Smoothing multiplier on the KDE's auto (Silverman) bandwidth — >1 smoother, <1 wigglier. Unset reads as 1.

channelConfigs.r.histogram.densityFill.doc: Fill the area under the density curve (at reduced opacity). When false the overlay is a stroked line only.

channelConfigs.r.histogram.enabled.doc: Bin the quantitative category axis instead of treating each distinct value as its own bar.

channelConfigs.r.histogram.labelMode.doc: How each bin's axis label reads: - "range": the full span, e.g. "10 – 20" (default). - "low": only the bin's lower edge, e.g. "10". - "high": only the bin's upper edge, e.g. "20".

channelConfigs.r.histogram.mode.doc: What the bars (and the opposite axis) represent: - "count": raw row count per bin. - "density": each bin's share of the total (count / total), so values fall in 0–1 and sum to 1 (relative frequency). Computed per facet panel when faceted.

channelConfigs.r.histogram.rugColor.doc: Single rug-tick color, used when no `rugPalette` is picked (or no hue is mapped to color the ticks per category).

channelConfigs.r.histogram.rugPaletteId.doc: Optional saved palette id for the rug. When set (paired with the snapshotted `rugPalette` colors) AND a hue field is mapped, each tick is colored by its hue category via `rugPalette[i mod n]` (categories in hue-scale order). `null` → every tick uses the single `rugColor`.

channelConfigs.r.histogram.rugTickLength.doc: Total length (px) of each rug tick, centered on the axis baseline (half above, half below). Unset → default tick length.

channelConfigs.r.histogram.rugTickThickn.doc: Thickness (px) of each rug tick's stroke. Unset → default thickness.

channelConfigs.r.histogram.showDensity.doc: Overlay a smooth density curve (Gaussian KDE) on top of the bars, rescaled into the bars' units (count or relative frequency) so it tracks their heights. A bin-independent read of the distribution's shape. Off by default; optional so older saves load unchanged.

channelConfigs.r.histogram.showRug.doc: Show a rug: one short tick per raw row drawn along the binned axis at the row's exact value — vertical ticks on an x-axis histogram, horizontal on a y-axis one. A density read that complements the bars. This is the histogram form of the strip plot's "show points". Off by default.

channelConfigs.r.jitterAmount.doc: Random horizontal/vertical offset applied to scatter points along *this* axis when it's the categorical side of a strip plot. Expressed as a fraction of the per-category band width: 0 = no jitter (default), 1 = fills the full band. Ignored on quantitative/temporal axes.

channelConfigs.r.jitterOverlappingOnly.doc: "Only jitter overlapping points": when true, `jitterAmount` moves only the points that share their exact pre-jitter position (same category AND same value) with at least one other point; a point that sits alone stays on the band center. Absent / false (default) jitters every point.

channelConfigs.r.min.doc: User-pinned domain bounds for a continuous (quantitative / temporal) axis. `null` / absent means "auto-fit from the data" (the default). Quantitative axes store the raw value; temporal axes store epoch milliseconds. Ignored on categorical / ordinal-string axes.

channelConfigs.r.mirror.doc: "Use a mirrored axis" (Ticks section, bar measure axis only): the measure axis runs through 0 with a category's bars split to either side by a two-level direction field — expenses left / profit right, males left / females right — while the underlying counts stay positive. See `MirrorAxisConfig`.

channelConfigs.r.mirror.breaks.doc: Custom tick breaks as MAGNITUDES, mirrored to both sides: `[50, 100]` pins ticks at -100, -50, 50, 100 (0 pins once). Replaces the plain `breaks` list while the mirror is on; same additive-to-auto semantics.

channelConfigs.r.mirror.directionField.doc: Two-level field deciding which side each row's bar goes to. `null` = not chosen yet.

channelConfigs.r.mirror.negativeMax.doc: Magnitude the NEGATIVE side extends to ("Left max" / "Lower max"). Stored positive; the domain min becomes `-negativeMax`. Blank / absent = auto-fit from the data on that side.

channelConfigs.r.mirror.positiveMax.doc: Magnitude the POSITIVE side extends to ("Right max" / "Upper max"). Blank / absent = auto-fit.

channelConfigs.r.offset.doc: LEGACY perpendicular nudge (px) that moves the axis tick labels closer to or farther from the plot area. Positive pushes them AWAY from the plot (an x-axis moves vertically, a y-axis horizontally).

channelConfigs.r.offsetX.doc: "Adjust position" nudge (px, screen coords: +x right, +y down) applied to the TICK LABELS only — the control lives in the Tick Labels section, so the spine, tick marks, title, and gridlines all stay put.

channelConfigs.r.regression.doc: Regression-line overlay for a two-quantitative scatter. Only ever set on the X axis config (fits are y-on-x). Optional so saved visuals load unchanged — absent reads as disabled.

channelConfigs.r.regression.ciFillColor.doc: CI band fill fallback, same role as `color` for the band. Theme-seeded (theme.regressionCiFill).

channelConfigs.r.regression.color.doc: Line stroke fallback when the Regression line color slot isn't set and no hue inheritance applies. Theme-seeded (theme.regressionStroke).

channelConfigs.r.regression.customDashar.doc: User-typed SVG dasharray (e.g. "2,2"). Wins over `lineStyle` when set; unparseable input falls back to `lineStyle` (mirrors the per-category `customDashOverrides` semantics).

channelConfigs.r.regression.dashRange.doc: Gate the dash to an x-range (solid outside). Independent of the connection channel's `dashRange` — the regression line's dash is its own setting, so its range is too.

channelConfigs.r.regression.degree.doc: Polynomial degree (only read when kind === "polynomial"). Clamped 2–6.

channelConfigs.r.regression.drawPosition.doc: Draw the line (and CI band) in front of or behind the dots.

channelConfigs.r.regression.groupField.doc: Grouping variable for per-group fits. Pre-filled from the hue field (when mapped) at the moment "Line per group" is enabled.

channelConfigs.r.regression.lineStyle.doc: Line dash — same options regular connection lines get (recipes in `lib/dashPatterns.ts`). Set from the Pattern menu's "Regression line" subheader. Ignored when `customDasharray` is set.

channelConfigs.r.regression.perGroup.doc: Fit one line per value of `groupField` instead of a single pooled line. When on with no `groupField` chosen yet, the pooled line draws.

channelConfigs.r.regression.showCi.doc: Draw a pointwise confidence band for the mean response.

channelConfigs.r.side.doc: Plot edge the whole axis — spine, tick marks, tick labels and title — sits on ("Side" in the Spine section). x: "bottom" (default) or "top"; y: "left" (default) or "right". Absent = the default edge; see `axisFlipped`.

channelConfigs.r.spine.opacity.doc: Stroke opacity [0,1]. Only the radar spoke spine reads this (the R position menu's Spine section); cartesian axis spines leave it unset. Sparse: absent = 1.

channelConfigs.r.spineAtZero.doc: "Set spine at 0": draw THIS axis's spine where the PERPENDICULAR axis's scale crosses 0, instead of at the plot edge — with negative values along x, checking it on the Y panel moves the vertical spine from the left edge to x = 0 (and on X, drops the horizontal spine to y = 0 when y has negatives).

channelConfigs.r.tickLabelAngle.doc: Tick label rotation in degrees, clockwise around each tick's anchor. `null` (the default) = AUTO: a categorical / ordinal x-axis rotates to -45° when neighboring labels would collide (`lib/autoLabelAngle.ts`), every other axis stays level.

channelConfigs.r.tickLabelColor.doc: Per-axis tick LABEL color. Superseded by `tickLabelFont.color` when that is set; kept for back-compat with visuals saved before the fuller `tickLabelFont` override existed. When neither is set, tick labels inherit the global Text encoding color (`labels.baseFont.text.color`).

channelConfigs.r.tickLabelColorRules.doc: Conditional tick-label colors ("+ Add color rule" under the Tick labels Color row on the x / y panels).

channelConfigs.r.tickLabelFont.doc: Per-axis tick LABEL font override. Any subset of family / size / color / weight / italic / underline may be set; unset fields fall through to the global Text encoding font (`labels.baseFont.text`). Lets the user style an individual axis's tick labels independently — e.g. a smaller monospace y-axis.

channelConfigs.r.wrapTickLabelAlign.doc: Tick-label alignment ("Align" in the Tick labels section; the field keeps its historical name from when it applied to wrapped labels only).

channelConfigs.r.wrapTickLabelChars.doc: "Characters" under Wrap text: a target line length in characters. When set, tick labels wrap at the space / internal hyphen NEAREST that count (`wrapByCharCount`, the Data Labels rule) instead of filling the axis's pixel budget, and a single over-long word stays whole.

channelConfigs.r.wrapTickLabels.doc: Line-wrap long tick labels ("Wrap text" in the Tick Labels section). X-axis labels wrap to their per-tick slot width; y / r labels wrap to a fixed font-relative max width (see `lib/tickLabelWrap.ts`). Wraps on spaces, hard-breaking a word only when it alone exceeds a line.

channelConfigs.saturation.min.doc: Anchored levels, NOT absolute HSL components: 0.5 leaves the base color's saturation alone, 0 is fully gray, 1 fully saturated. See `anchoredComponent` in lib/scales.

channelConfigs.saturation.overrides.doc: Per-value overrides, keyed by the value's string form: a category of a categorical/ordinal field mapped to the channel, or a packed-circles derived value (a depth level "1"/"2"/… or a top-level group name). An unset value falls back to the even min→max spread.

channelConfigs.saturationSlots.doc: Per-part saturation targets (outline / line) beyond the Fill, which reuses the `saturation` encoding. Sparse — an absent slot means that part isn't modulated. Surfaced as subheaders in the Saturation menu.

channelConfigs.shape.customGlyphs.doc: Per-chart custom glyphs. A shape index `i >= CUSTOM_GLYPH_BASE` (lib/customGlyphs) refers to `customGlyphs[i - CUSTOM_GLYPH_BASE]`. The base is a fixed constant past the built-in palette, so appending a built-in symbol never shifts these references.

channelConfigs.shape.customGlyphs[].dx.doc: Optional position nudge set at glyph creation, in multiples of the mark's circle-equivalent radius (screen convention: positive `dy` = down). Lets a glyph branch off the data point — e.g. an OHLC open/close tick pushed clear of the connection line. Absent = centered.

channelConfigs.shape.distributionOutline.doc: Stroke width (px) of the violin outline and all box strokes (body, whiskers, caps, outlier circles) when a distribution overlay is on; the median line draws at 1.5× this for emphasis. Its own knob, deliberately independent of `outlineWidth` (which the point marks read). 0 hides the borders.

channelConfigs.shape.fillOverrides.doc: Per-category override for the mark's fill color. Wins over the encoding's hue color for that category — useful when the user wants one specific category to render hollow ("none"), pair a light fill with a dark outline, etc. Keyed by stringified category value.

channelConfigs.shape.outlineColor.doc: Stroke color applied to every point mark. Seeded from the theme's `outlineColor` on chart creation; users can override per-chart in the Shape panel.

channelConfigs.shape.outlineColorRules.doc: Conditional outline-color rules, evaluated against the mapped `outlineHue` variable's value for each mark (mirrors Data Labels' `textColorRules`). First matching rule wins and overrides the outlineHue scale color; per-category `strokeOverrides` still win on top.

channelConfigs.shape.outlineWidth.doc: Stroke width in pixels applied to every point mark. `0` hides the outline entirely.

channelConfigs.shape.strokeOverrides.doc: Per-category override for the mark's stroke color. Same precedence as `fillOverrides` but for the outline. Empty / absent → falls back to the global `outlineColor`.

channelConfigs.text.color.doc: Single fallback color when neither a palette nor a per-category override applies.

channelConfigs.text.colorOverrides.doc: Per-category color overrides, keyed by stringified category value. Always wins when set, regardless of palette / fallback.

channelConfigs.text.decimals.doc: Number of fractional digits when the text value is numeric. `null` leaves numbers as the raw string from the row.

channelConfigs.text.palette.doc: Optional palette assigned to the text channel — independent from the hue palette so e.g. light-fill bars can carry darker text via a paired darker palette. When null/empty, text falls back to the single `color` fallback.

channelConfigs.x.histogram.showRug.doc: Show a rug: one short tick per raw row drawn along the binned axis at the row's exact value — vertical ticks on an x-axis histogram, horizontal on a y-axis one.
