channelConfigs.x.jitterAmount.doc: Random horizontal/vertical offset applied to scatter points along *this* axis when it's the categorical side of a strip plot. Expressed as a fraction of the per-category band width: 0 = no jitter (default), 1 = fills the full band. Ignored on quantitative/temporal axes.

channelConfigs.x.jitterOverlappingOnly.doc: "Only jitter overlapping points": when true, `jitterAmount` moves only the points that share their exact pre-jitter position (same category AND same value) with at least one other point; a point that sits alone stays on the band center. Absent / false (default) jitters every point.

channelConfigs.x.min.doc: User-pinned domain bounds for a continuous (quantitative / temporal) axis. `null` / absent means "auto-fit from the data" (the default). Quantitative axes store the raw value; temporal axes store epoch milliseconds. Ignored on categorical / ordinal-string axes.

channelConfigs.x.mirror.doc: "Use a mirrored axis" (Ticks section, bar measure axis only): the measure axis runs through 0 with a category's bars split to either side by a two-level direction field — expenses left / profit right, males left / females right — while the underlying counts stay positive. See `MirrorAxisConfig`.

channelConfigs.x.mirror.breaks.doc: Custom tick breaks as MAGNITUDES, mirrored to both sides: `[50, 100]` pins ticks at -100, -50, 50, 100 (0 pins once). Replaces the plain `breaks` list while the mirror is on; same additive-to-auto semantics.

channelConfigs.x.mirror.directionField.doc: Two-level field deciding which side each row's bar goes to. `null` = not chosen yet.

channelConfigs.x.mirror.negativeMax.doc: Magnitude the NEGATIVE side extends to ("Left max" / "Lower max"). Stored positive; the domain min becomes `-negativeMax`. Blank / absent = auto-fit from the data on that side.

channelConfigs.x.mirror.positiveMax.doc: Magnitude the POSITIVE side extends to ("Right max" / "Upper max"). Blank / absent = auto-fit.

channelConfigs.x.offset.doc: LEGACY perpendicular nudge (px) that moves the axis tick labels closer to or farther from the plot area. Positive pushes them AWAY from the plot (an x-axis moves vertically, a y-axis horizontally).

channelConfigs.x.offsetX.doc: "Adjust position" nudge (px, screen coords: +x right, +y down) applied to the TICK LABELS only — the control lives in the Tick Labels section, so the spine, tick marks, title, and gridlines all stay put.

channelConfigs.x.regression.doc: Regression-line overlay for a two-quantitative scatter. Only ever set on the X axis config (fits are y-on-x). Optional so saved visuals load unchanged — absent reads as disabled.

channelConfigs.x.regression.ciFillColor.doc: CI band fill fallback, same role as `color` for the band. Theme-seeded (theme.regressionCiFill).

channelConfigs.x.regression.color.doc: Line stroke fallback when the Regression line color slot isn't set and no hue inheritance applies. Theme-seeded (theme.regressionStroke).

channelConfigs.x.regression.customDashar.doc: User-typed SVG dasharray (e.g. "2,2"). Wins over `lineStyle` when set; unparseable input falls back to `lineStyle` (mirrors the per-category `customDashOverrides` semantics).

channelConfigs.x.regression.dashRange.doc: Gate the dash to an x-range (solid outside). Independent of the connection channel's `dashRange` — the regression line's dash is its own setting, so its range is too.

channelConfigs.x.regression.degree.doc: Polynomial degree (only read when kind === "polynomial"). Clamped 2–6.

channelConfigs.x.regression.drawPosition.doc: Draw the line (and CI band) in front of or behind the dots.

channelConfigs.x.regression.groupField.doc: Grouping variable for per-group fits. Pre-filled from the hue field (when mapped) at the moment "Line per group" is enabled.

channelConfigs.x.regression.lineStyle.doc: Line dash — same options regular connection lines get (recipes in `lib/dashPatterns.ts`). Set from the Pattern menu's "Regression line" subheader. Ignored when `customDasharray` is set.

channelConfigs.x.regression.perGroup.doc: Fit one line per value of `groupField` instead of a single pooled line. When on with no `groupField` chosen yet, the pooled line draws.

channelConfigs.x.regression.showCi.doc: Draw a pointwise confidence band for the mean response.

channelConfigs.x.side.doc: Plot edge the whole axis — spine, tick marks, tick labels and title — sits on ("Side" in the Spine section). x: "bottom" (default) or "top"; y: "left" (default) or "right". Absent = the default edge; see `axisFlipped`.

channelConfigs.x.spine.opacity.doc: Stroke opacity [0,1]. Only the radar spoke spine reads this (the R position menu's Spine section); cartesian axis spines leave it unset. Sparse: absent = 1.

channelConfigs.x.spineAtZero.doc: "Set spine at 0": draw THIS axis's spine where the PERPENDICULAR axis's scale crosses 0, instead of at the plot edge — with negative values along x, checking it on the Y panel moves the vertical spine from the left edge to x = 0 (and on X, drops the horizontal spine to y = 0 when y has negatives).

channelConfigs.x.tickLabelAngle.doc: Tick label rotation in degrees, clockwise around each tick's anchor. `null` (the default) = AUTO: a categorical / ordinal x-axis rotates to -45° when neighboring labels would collide (`lib/autoLabelAngle.ts`), every other axis stays level.

channelConfigs.x.tickLabelColor.doc: Per-axis tick LABEL color. Superseded by `tickLabelFont.color` when that is set; kept for back-compat with visuals saved before the fuller `tickLabelFont` override existed. When neither is set, tick labels inherit the global Text encoding color (`labels.baseFont.text.color`).

channelConfigs.x.tickLabelColorRules.doc: Conditional tick-label colors ("+ Add color rule" under the Tick labels Color row on the x / y panels).

channelConfigs.x.tickLabelFont.doc: Per-axis tick LABEL font override. Any subset of family / size / color / weight / italic / underline may be set; unset fields fall through to the global Text encoding font (`labels.baseFont.text`). Lets the user style an individual axis's tick labels independently — e.g. a smaller monospace y-axis.

channelConfigs.x.wrapTickLabelAlign.doc: Tick-label alignment ("Align" in the Tick labels section; the field keeps its historical name from when it applied to wrapped labels only).

channelConfigs.x.wrapTickLabelChars.doc: "Characters" under Wrap text: a target line length in characters. When set, tick labels wrap at the space / internal hyphen NEAREST that count (`wrapByCharCount`, the Data Labels rule) instead of filling the axis's pixel budget, and a single over-long word stays whole.

channelConfigs.x.wrapTickLabels.doc: Line-wrap long tick labels ("Wrap text" in the Tick Labels section). X-axis labels wrap to their per-tick slot width; y / r labels wrap to a fixed font-relative max width (see `lib/tickLabelWrap.ts`). Wraps on spaces, hard-breaking a word only when it alone exceeds a line.

channelConfigs.y.breaks.doc: Extra pinned tick positions for a continuous axis, ADDED to the auto `tickCount` layout (set `tickCount: 0` and list breaks for fully custom ticks). Tick labels follow the ticks — every tick gets a label. Empty / absent = auto only. Numbers are axis values (epoch ms for temporal).

channelConfigs.y.categoricalTickStride.doc: Stride between visible ticks on a categorical/ordinal axis. `1` (the default) shows every category. `2` shows every other, `3` every third, etc. — useful when there are too many categories to label each one cleanly. The first and last categories always render so the axis ends stay anchored.

channelConfigs.y.customFormat.doc: d3-format (quantitative) or d3-time-format (temporal) string. Empty string means "use the scale's default formatter". The sidebar exposes a dropdown of presets that populate this field; the user can refine the resulting spec by hand.

channelConfigs.y.distributionOverlay.doc: Distribution overlays — meaningful only when this axis is quantitative and the other axis is categorical.

channelConfigs.y.distributionOverlay.box.doc: Multiplier on the box's thickness — the fat dimension perpendicular to the value axis (horizontal for a vertical box, vertical for a horizontal one). 1 = the default (a box spanning ~36% of the category band); larger makes the box fatter/taller, smaller makes it skinnier.

channelConfigs.y.distributionOverlay.col.doc: Stroke color used when hue isn't mapped (so there's no per-category palette to inherit from) and no per-category override exists.
Per-category stroke overrides keyed by stringified category value. Wins over hue inheritance and the default `color`.

channelConfigs.y.distributionOverlay.fil.doc: Fill color (with reduced opacity) under the same conditions.
Per-category fill overrides. Same precedence as `colorOverrides` for fills.

channelConfigs.y.distributionOverlay.mar.doc: Box plot only, and only while `showPoints` is false: draw one point per box at the category's arithmetic mean.

channelConfigs.y.distributionOverlay.sho.doc: Render a Tukey box (q1/median/q3 + 1.5*IQR whiskers + outliers) per category.

Render a standalone density curve — a single KDE line rising from the axis baseline (not mirrored like a violin). Only meaningful in the single-quantitative-variable case (the same situation a histogram applies), so it's surfaced as a sibling of Histogram in the Distribution control.
Render a mirrored KDE polygon per category.
When false, the underlying scatter marks are hidden so the overlay stands alone (classic violin-only / box-only plot). Defaults to true so enabling an overlay on a strip plot keeps the dots visible.

channelConfigs.y.gridlines.breaks.doc: User-pinned gridline positions on a continuous axis — the gridline counterpart of `AxisConfig.breaks`. Plain axis values (epoch-ms for temporal). When non-empty these win over `count` entirely. Optional so visuals saved before it existed load unchanged.

channelConfigs.y.gridlines.count.doc: Gridline count. `null` means "match the axis tick count" (one gridline per labeled tick) — this is the default and what users most often want. Set to a specific number to decouple from ticks.

channelConfigs.y.histogram.doc: Histogram binning for a quantitative category axis in bar charts. Absent / `enabled: false` means "no binning" (the default). Optional so existing saved configs load unchanged — a missing value reads as disabled.

channelConfigs.y.histogram.binCount.doc: Number of equal-width bins. Clamped to >= 1 at render time.

channelConfigs.y.histogram.densityBandwi.doc: Smoothing multiplier on the KDE's auto (Silverman) bandwidth — >1 smoother, <1 wigglier. Unset reads as 1.

channelConfigs.y.histogram.densityFill.doc: Fill the area under the density curve (at reduced opacity). When false the overlay is a stroked line only.

channelConfigs.y.histogram.enabled.doc: Bin the quantitative category axis instead of treating each distinct value as its own bar.

channelConfigs.y.histogram.labelMode.doc: How each bin's axis label reads: - "range": the full span, e.g. "10 – 20" (default). - "low": only the bin's lower edge, e.g. "10". - "high": only the bin's upper edge, e.g. "20".

channelConfigs.y.histogram.mode.doc: What the bars (and the opposite axis) represent: - "count": raw row count per bin. - "density": each bin's share of the total (count / total), so values fall in 0–1 and sum to 1 (relative frequency). Computed per facet panel when faceted.

channelConfigs.y.histogram.rugColor.doc: Single rug-tick color, used when no `rugPalette` is picked (or no hue is mapped to color the ticks per category).

channelConfigs.y.histogram.rugPaletteId.doc: Optional saved palette id for the rug. When set (paired with the snapshotted `rugPalette` colors) AND a hue field is mapped, each tick is colored by its hue category via `rugPalette[i mod n]` (categories in hue-scale order). `null` → every tick uses the single `rugColor`.

channelConfigs.y.histogram.rugTickLength.doc: Total length (px) of each rug tick, centered on the axis baseline (half above, half below). Unset → default tick length.

channelConfigs.y.histogram.rugTickThickn.doc: Thickness (px) of each rug tick's stroke. Unset → default thickness.

channelConfigs.y.histogram.showDensity.doc: Overlay a smooth density curve (Gaussian KDE) on top of the bars, rescaled into the bars' units (count or relative frequency) so it tracks their heights. A bin-independent read of the distribution's shape. Off by default; optional so older saves load unchanged.

channelConfigs.y.histogram.showRug.doc: Show a rug: one short tick per raw row drawn along the binned axis at the row's exact value — vertical ticks on an x-axis histogram, horizontal on a y-axis one. A density read that complements the bars. This is the histogram form of the strip plot's "show points". Off by default.

channelConfigs.y.jitterAmount.doc: Random horizontal/vertical offset applied to scatter points along *this* axis when it's the categorical side of a strip plot. Expressed as a fraction of the per-category band width: 0 = no jitter (default), 1 = fills the full band. Ignored on quantitative/temporal axes.

channelConfigs.y.jitterOverlappingOnly.doc: "Only jitter overlapping points": when true, `jitterAmount` moves only the points that share their exact pre-jitter position (same category AND same value) with at least one other point; a point that sits alone stays on the band center. Absent / false (default) jitters every point.

channelConfigs.y.min.doc: User-pinned domain bounds for a continuous (quantitative / temporal) axis. `null` / absent means "auto-fit from the data" (the default). Quantitative axes store the raw value; temporal axes store epoch milliseconds. Ignored on categorical / ordinal-string axes.

channelConfigs.y.mirror.doc: "Use a mirrored axis" (Ticks section, bar measure axis only): the measure axis runs through 0 with a category's bars split to either side by a two-level direction field — expenses left / profit right, males left / females right — while the underlying counts stay positive. See `MirrorAxisConfig`.

channelConfigs.y.mirror.breaks.doc: Custom tick breaks as MAGNITUDES, mirrored to both sides: `[50, 100]` pins ticks at -100, -50, 50, 100 (0 pins once). Replaces the plain `breaks` list while the mirror is on; same additive-to-auto semantics.

channelConfigs.y.mirror.directionField.doc: Two-level field deciding which side each row's bar goes to. `null` = not chosen yet.

channelConfigs.y.mirror.negativeMax.doc: Magnitude the NEGATIVE side extends to ("Left max" / "Lower max"). Stored positive; the domain min becomes `-negativeMax`. Blank / absent = auto-fit from the data on that side.

channelConfigs.y.mirror.positiveMax.doc: Magnitude the POSITIVE side extends to ("Right max" / "Upper max"). Blank / absent = auto-fit.

channelConfigs.y.offset.doc: LEGACY perpendicular nudge (px) that moves the axis tick labels closer to or farther from the plot area. Positive pushes them AWAY from the plot (an x-axis moves vertically, a y-axis horizontally).

channelConfigs.y.offsetX.doc: "Adjust position" nudge (px, screen coords: +x right, +y down) applied to the TICK LABELS only — the control lives in the Tick Labels section, so the spine, tick marks, title, and gridlines all stay put.

channelConfigs.y.regression.doc: Regression-line overlay for a two-quantitative scatter. Only ever set on the X axis config (fits are y-on-x). Optional so saved visuals load unchanged — absent reads as disabled.

channelConfigs.y.regression.ciFillColor.doc: CI band fill fallback, same role as `color` for the band. Theme-seeded (theme.regressionCiFill).

channelConfigs.y.regression.color.doc: Line stroke fallback when the Regression line color slot isn't set and no hue inheritance applies. Theme-seeded (theme.regressionStroke).

channelConfigs.y.regression.customDashar.doc: User-typed SVG dasharray (e.g. "2,2"). Wins over `lineStyle` when set; unparseable input falls back to `lineStyle` (mirrors the per-category `customDashOverrides` semantics).

channelConfigs.y.regression.dashRange.doc: Gate the dash to an x-range (solid outside). Independent of the connection channel's `dashRange` — the regression line's dash is its own setting, so its range is too.

channelConfigs.y.regression.degree.doc: Polynomial degree (only read when kind === "polynomial"). Clamped 2–6.

channelConfigs.y.regression.drawPosition.doc: Draw the line (and CI band) in front of or behind the dots.

channelConfigs.y.regression.groupField.doc: Grouping variable for per-group fits. Pre-filled from the hue field (when mapped) at the moment "Line per group" is enabled.

channelConfigs.y.regression.lineStyle.doc: Line dash — same options regular connection lines get (recipes in `lib/dashPatterns.ts`). Set from the Pattern menu's "Regression line" subheader. Ignored when `customDasharray` is set.

channelConfigs.y.regression.perGroup.doc: Fit one line per value of `groupField` instead of a single pooled line. When on with no `groupField` chosen yet, the pooled line draws.

channelConfigs.y.regression.showCi.doc: Draw a pointwise confidence band for the mean response.

channelConfigs.y.side.doc: Plot edge the whole axis — spine, tick marks, tick labels and title — sits on ("Side" in the Spine section). x: "bottom" (default) or "top"; y: "left" (default) or "right". Absent = the default edge; see `axisFlipped`.

channelConfigs.y.spine.opacity.doc: Stroke opacity [0,1]. Only the radar spoke spine reads this (the R position menu's Spine section); cartesian axis spines leave it unset. Sparse: absent = 1.

channelConfigs.y.spineAtZero.doc: "Set spine at 0": draw THIS axis's spine where the PERPENDICULAR axis's scale crosses 0, instead of at the plot edge — with negative values along x, checking it on the Y panel moves the vertical spine from the left edge to x = 0 (and on X, drops the horizontal spine to y = 0 when y has negatives).

channelConfigs.y.tickLabelAngle.doc: Tick label rotation in degrees, clockwise around each tick's anchor. `null` (the default) = AUTO: a categorical / ordinal x-axis rotates to -45° when neighboring labels would collide (`lib/autoLabelAngle.ts`), every other axis stays level.

channelConfigs.y.tickLabelColor.doc: Per-axis tick LABEL color. Superseded by `tickLabelFont.color` when that is set; kept for back-compat with visuals saved before the fuller `tickLabelFont` override existed. When neither is set, tick labels inherit the global Text encoding color (`labels.baseFont.text.color`).

channelConfigs.y.tickLabelColorRules.doc: Conditional tick-label colors ("+ Add color rule" under the Tick labels Color row on the x / y panels).

channelConfigs.y.tickLabelFont.doc: Per-axis tick LABEL font override. Any subset of family / size / color / weight / italic / underline may be set; unset fields fall through to the global Text encoding font (`labels.baseFont.text`). Lets the user style an individual axis's tick labels independently — e.g. a smaller monospace y-axis.

channelConfigs.y.wrapTickLabelAlign.doc: Tick-label alignment ("Align" in the Tick labels section; the field keeps its historical name from when it applied to wrapped labels only).

channelConfigs.y.wrapTickLabelChars.doc: "Characters" under Wrap text: a target line length in characters. When set, tick labels wrap at the space / internal hyphen NEAREST that count (`wrapByCharCount`, the Data Labels rule) instead of filling the axis's pixel budget, and a single over-long word stays whole.

channelConfigs.y.wrapTickLabels.doc: Line-wrap long tick labels ("Wrap text" in the Tick Labels section). X-axis labels wrap to their per-tick slot width; y / r labels wrap to a fixed font-relative max width (see `lib/tickLabelWrap.ts`). Wraps on spaces, hard-breaking a word only when it alone exceeds a line.

dataLabelsConfig.doc: Per-visual Data Labels appearance + offsets + scale knobs. Optional for back-compat.

dataLabelsConfig.alignment.doc: Horizontal text alignment for the label. Maps to SVG `text-anchor`: - `center` (default) → `middle` (label centered on anchor point) - `left` → `start` (label extends right of anchor) - `right` → `end` (label extends left of anchor) Pairs naturally with `onlyLastLabel`: setting alignment to "left" +…

dataLabelsConfig.arcWrapLevels.doc: Packed circles only: container depths (1 = top level) whose labels wrap around the OUTSIDE of their circle on an arc instead of sitting inside the top rim. Managed by the Data Labels panel's "Text Position" checkboxes; other renderers ignore it.

dataLabelsConfig.areaLabelPosition.doc: Where labels sit along an area layer's measure axis, when the chart is an area chart. The layer runs from its base (the zero baseline, or the cumulative bottom of a stacked layer) to its top edge (the line). - `"edge"` (default): ON the layer's top edge — where the line is.

dataLabelsConfig.avoidOverlaps.doc: When true, the renderer detects label boxes that overlap and nudges later labels along the y-axis to keep them readable. Best-effort — with many labels in a small space some collisions remain — but cheap to enable when it helps.

dataLabelsConfig.barLabelPosition.doc: Where labels sit along a bar's measure axis, when the chart is a bar chart and Data Labels' position-axis isn't mapped to a field. - `"center"` (default): slice midpoint — current behavior. - `"inside-base"`: just inside the bar near the zero baseline / stack-bottom for stacked bars.

dataLabelsConfig.barLabelSide.doc: Which side of the bar labels sit on, ACROSS the category axis (bars only). Sparse — absent = `"center"`. - `"center"` (default): on the bar's category center. - `"before"`: just past the bar's leading edge — LEFT of a vertical bar, ABOVE a horizontal one.

dataLabelsConfig.color.doc: Fallback color used when no `hue` field is mapped (or no palette resolves).

dataLabelsConfig.colorOverrides.doc: Per-category color overrides keyed by stringified value of the hue field. Wins over the hue scale and the fallback.

dataLabelsConfig.combineVariables.doc: Multi-field mode only: whether the selected variables COMBINE into one label per anchor (the default — arranged by `labelTemplate` and the per-population templates) or each variable renders as its OWN label at the anchor (`false`).

dataLabelsConfig.composedLabels.doc: Multi-field mode: THE labels — one entry per text box under Value → Compose labels, each its own label at every anchor its "Which labels" names, composed with its template and keyed by its id in every per-label map (see `ComposedLabel`).

dataLabelsConfig.decimals.doc: When the text field is numeric, render with this many fractional digits. `null` leaves the raw value as-is. In multi-field mode this is the fallback for any selected field without its own `fieldFormats` entry.

dataLabelsConfig.facetKeys.doc: Faceted charts only: which panels draw labels. `null` / unset = every panel ("Label all facets", the default).

dataLabelsConfig.fieldAlignments.doc: Separate-variables mode only (`combineVariables === false`, where each variable is its own label): per-variable horizontal alignment, keyed by field name. Unset → the layer-wide `alignment`.

dataLabelsConfig.fieldBackgrounds.doc: Multi-field mode only: per-field text background, keyed by field name. `textBackground` null / unset follows the layer-wide toggle; `true` / `false` show / hide a background behind THAT variable's text regardless of it.

dataLabelsConfig.fieldBarPlacements.doc: Separate-variables mode only (`combineVariables === false`, where each variable is its own label on a bar): per-variable bar placement, keyed by field name — each variable's own measure-axis position and / or side, so e.g.

dataLabelsConfig.fieldColorRules.doc: Multi-field mode only: per-field TEXT COLOR RULES, keyed by field name — the same conditional rules as `textColorRules`, but evaluated against THAT variable's own value (the base rules compare against the label's primary value).

dataLabelsConfig.fieldColors.doc: Multi-field mode only: TEXT COLOR per composed label, keyed by the label's id — one color slot per label, mirroring the mark color slots (fill / outline / line).

dataLabelsConfig.fieldColors.*.colorRule.doc: Conditional color rules (the Color menu's "+ Add color rule" rows; the Line slot is the one that surfaces them). An implicit rule (`> 0`) tests the slot's mapped variable's value; a `{Variable}` rule tests that variable in the mark's rows.

dataLabelsConfig.fieldColors.*.field.doc: Dataset column driving this slot's color, or null = single color.

dataLabelsConfig.fieldColors.*.hue.doc: Reuses the hue union (categorical {colors} | quantitative gradient). NOTE: `stackMode` inside this union is inert for slots — never feed a slot's stackMode to `resolveStackMode`; only `hue`/`pattern` own layout.

dataLabelsConfig.fieldColors.*.hue.custo.doc: N-stop user-defined custom gradient — read only when palette is `"custom"`. The first/last stops anchor the gradient; any number of additional middle stops are allowed. The legacy `lowColor`/`midColor`/`highColor` fields stay for backwards compatibility with saved charts that pre-date this field.

dataLabelsConfig.fieldColors.*.hue.inter.doc: Color space used to blend between gradient stops — "rgb" (matches CSS gradients), "hsb", or "oklch" (perceptually uniform). Read only by the custom-gradient paths (customLinear / customDiverging / manual stops); presets are fully-specified ramps with nothing left to blend.

dataLabelsConfig.fieldColors.*.hue.sourc.doc: Records the dropdown selection that originated this config — a preset name (`"viridis"`), a saved gradient ID, `"custom"`, etc. Survives color edits so a "Reset colors" action can re-resolve to the originating palette's defaults instead of switching the whole palette type.

dataLabelsConfig.fieldColors.*.singleCol.doc: The "None" single color, theme-seeded per slot.

dataLabelsConfig.fieldFacetKeys.doc: Multi-field mode only: per-composed-label facet scope, keyed by the label's id — one label can draw on every panel while another is kept to a few.

dataLabelsConfig.fieldFonts.doc: Multi-field mode only: text properties (family / weight / italic / underline) per composed label, keyed by the label's id. Every key left unset inherits the layer-wide value, so a sparse `{ fontWeight: 700 }` bolds one label and changes nothing else.

dataLabelsConfig.fieldFormats.doc: Multi-field mode only: per-field number format, keyed by field name. Each value is a d3-format spec (the same specs the axes use, via `buildTickFormatter`) — e.g. `".1%"` → `32.0%`, `"$,.0f"` → `$1,200`. A field with no entry falls back to `decimals`.

dataLabelsConfig.fieldLabelPoints.doc: Multi-field mode only: per-variable "Which labels" selection, keyed by field name. A field with no entry falls back to `labelPoints` (via `fieldLabelPointsMode`).

dataLabelsConfig.fieldLabelPointsScope.doc: Multi-field mode only: per-composed-label "Of each" scope, keyed by the label's id — each label's series ends can run over a different unit (the `{value}` label on the last bar of each STACK, the `{series}` label on the last bar of each SERIES).

dataLabelsConfig.fieldLayers.doc: Bar + marks combos only: which layer each label annotates, keyed by label key (a composed label's id; the single-field label keys by its value field).

dataLabelsConfig.fieldLayouts.doc: Separate-variables mode only: per-variable text layout, keyed by field name — the variable's own angle, wrapping, and overlap avoidance. Unset keys inherit the layer-wide values.

dataLabelsConfig.fieldOffsets.doc: Separate-variables mode only: per-variable X / Y pixel nudges, keyed by field name — the variable's own base offsets (a matching position rule still replaces them). Unset keys → the layer-wide offsets.

dataLabelsConfig.fieldPolarPlacements.doc: Separate-variables mode only, on a pie: per-variable polar placement, keyed by field name — each variable's own angular nudge and / or radius, so e.g. the category name sits at the rim while the value sits inside the wedge. Unset keys inherit the layer-wide `polarLabelAngle` / `polarLabelRadius`.

dataLabelsConfig.fieldPositionRules.doc: Labels of their own (separate variables, combinations): each key's OWN conditional position rules — the per-label sibling of `positionRules`, which stays with the arranged label.

dataLabelsConfig.fieldSizes.doc: Multi-field mode only: font SIZE in POINTS per composed label, keyed by the label's id — so one label can render larger than another. A label with no entry takes `fontSize` (or the mapped Size scale when a size source is mapped).

dataLabelsConfig.firstLabel.doc: Per-endpoint overrides, consulted ONLY when two or more label populations coexist (`LabelSelection.split`): single-field `"first-last"`, or multi-field selections whose per-field modes name more than one of all / first / last.

dataLabelsConfig.firstLabel.alignment.doc: Replace the layer-wide alignment. null/unset = inherit.

dataLabelsConfig.firstLabel.labelTemplat.doc: Multi-field mode only: alternate `{Field}` template for this endpoint's labels. Empty/unset = inherit (see `populationTemplateFallback` in `lib/dataLabelsSelection.ts`: the shared `labelTemplate` when no all-labels population is using it, else this population's own fields joined with ", ").

dataLabelsConfig.firstLabel.xOffset.doc: REPLACE (not add to) the layer-wide xOffset/yOffset for this endpoint's labels. null/unset = inherit.

dataLabelsConfig.flowLabelNodes.doc: Flow diagrams (chord / sankey) only: which NODES get a label — by flow direction (`lib/flowNodeLabels`). Absent = every node. Applies to every composed label; `labelPoints` stands down on flows (no series).

dataLabelsConfig.fontFamily.doc: Font family for labels. Defaults to the theme's text font.

dataLabelsConfig.fontSize.doc: Default font size in px (used when no `size` field is mapped).

dataLabelsConfig.fontWeight.doc: Default font weight applied to every label (when no per-channel override applies).

dataLabelsConfig.gradientColors.doc: Resolved low/mid/high colors when `gradientId` points at a saved linear / diverging gradient. `null` when the id is a preset (those resolve via the d3 interpolator at render time).

dataLabelsConfig.gradientId.doc: Quantitative gradient id used when the hue field's effective type is quantitative/temporal. Either a d3 preset name (`"viridis"`, `"plasma"`, …) or a saved-gradient id from `theme.linearGradients` / `theme.divergingGradients`. `null` means no gradient — labels fall back to the single `color` value.

dataLabelsConfig.italic.doc: Italic label text. Optional so saved visuals from before the style controls load with it off — matching their previous look.

dataLabelsConfig.labelPoints.doc: Which labels render, per series. Supersedes `onlyLastLabel`; resolve the effective value via `effectiveLabelPoints(cfg)`, which falls back to the legacy boolean when this is unset. - `"all"` (default): every label.

dataLabelsConfig.labelPointsScope.doc: What the series ends ("first" / "last") run over on BAR charts. Layer-wide (the single-field label's scope, and the fallback for a composed label with no `fieldLabelPointsScope` entry): - "series" (default): the first / last category along the axis, per series — a series being the bar's stack + grou…

dataLabelsConfig.labelTemplate.doc: Multi-field mode only (`DataLabelsEncodings.value.multiField`): the arrangement of the selected fields, as a string with `{Field}` tokens — e.g. `"{Region} ({Share})"`. Any literal text between tokens is kept verbatim; a token whose name isn't a selected field is left as-is.

dataLabelsConfig.lastLabel.alignment.doc: Replace the layer-wide alignment. null/unset = inherit.

dataLabelsConfig.lastLabel.labelTemplate.doc: Multi-field mode only: alternate `{Field}` template for this endpoint's labels. Empty/unset = inherit (see `populationTemplateFallback` in `lib/dataLabelsSelection.ts`: the shared `labelTemplate` when no all-labels population is using it, else this population's own fields joined with ", ").

dataLabelsConfig.lastLabel.xOffset.doc: REPLACE (not add to) the layer-wide xOffset/yOffset for this endpoint's labels. null/unset = inherit.

dataLabelsConfig.leaderLineColor.doc: Stroke color of the leader lines. Theme-seeded (`Theme.mapLeaderLineColor`).

dataLabelsConfig.leaderLineWidth.doc: Stroke thickness (px) of the leader lines — 0 hides them. Theme-seeded (`Theme.mapLeaderLineThickness`).

dataLabelsConfig.leaderLines.doc: Maps only: draw a leader line from each region's centroid to its label whenever the label sits away from the centroid (X/Y offset or an overlap-avoidance nudge). A label still on its centroid draws no line. Non-geo renderers ignore it.

dataLabelsConfig.onlyLastLabel.doc: When true, only the LAST label per series is rendered — useful for directly labeling line charts and stacked bar charts at their end so the legend can be turned off. "Series" is the value of the hue field (anchor-based renderers) or the connection field (scatter+connection line charts).

dataLabelsConfig.palette.doc: Resolved palette colors — duplicated from `theme.categoricalPalettes` at the moment the user picks a palette so the renderer doesn't have to reach into the theme atom on every frame. Empty when no palette is selected.

dataLabelsConfig.paletteId.doc: Saved-palette id (from `theme.categoricalPalettes`) used to color labels by the hue field's category index. `null` means the user hasn't picked a labels-specific palette — the layer inherits the CHART's palette so labels match the marks without extra setup.

dataLabelsConfig.pieceSplits.doc: Multi-field mode only: which sections of a composed label are styled PER VARIABLE ("Split into individual variables"), keyed by the label's id. Unset / false = the label styles as one — every piece takes the label's own color / size / text properties.

dataLabelsConfig.pieces.doc: Multi-field mode only: the per-VARIABLE styling of split sections, keyed by the composed label's id and then the variable's name — two user strings kept as two keys, never joined into one (a joined key needs a separator no name can contain, which means a control character in saved content).

dataLabelsConfig.pieces.*.*.color.colorR.doc: Conditional color rules (the Color menu's "+ Add color rule" rows; the Line slot is the one that surfaces them). An implicit rule (`> 0`) tests the slot's mapped variable's value; a `{Variable}` rule tests that variable in the mark's rows.

dataLabelsConfig.pieces.*.*.color.field.doc: Dataset column driving this slot's color, or null = single color.

dataLabelsConfig.pieces.*.*.color.hue.doc: Reuses the hue union (categorical {colors} | quantitative gradient). NOTE: `stackMode` inside this union is inert for slots — never feed a slot's stackMode to `resolveStackMode`; only `hue`/`pattern` own layout.

dataLabelsConfig.pieces.*.*.color.hue.cu.doc: N-stop user-defined custom gradient — read only when palette is `"custom"`. The first/last stops anchor the gradient; any number of additional middle stops are allowed. The legacy `lowColor`/`midColor`/`highColor` fields stay for backwards compatibility with saved charts that pre-date this field.

dataLabelsConfig.pieces.*.*.color.hue.in.doc: Color space used to blend between gradient stops — "rgb" (matches CSS gradients), "hsb", or "oklch" (perceptually uniform). Read only by the custom-gradient paths (customLinear / customDiverging / manual stops); presets are fully-specified ramps with nothing left to blend.

dataLabelsConfig.pieces.*.*.color.hue.so.doc: Records the dropdown selection that originated this config — a preset name (`"viridis"`), a saved gradient ID, `"custom"`, etc. Survives color edits so a "Reset colors" action can re-resolve to the originating palette's defaults instead of switching the whole palette type.

dataLabelsConfig.pieces.*.*.color.single.doc: The "None" single color, theme-seeded per slot.

dataLabelsConfig.polarLabelAngle.doc: Pie / polar label placement — angular nudge in DEGREES applied to every label, rotating it off its slice's midpoint angle. Positive = clockwise, matching d3's arc convention (0° = 12 o'clock). The cartesian polar analogue of `xOffset`. Ignored by non-polar renderers.

dataLabelsConfig.polarLabelRadius.doc: Pie / polar label placement — distance from the pie center as a PERCENT of the pie radius. `100` (the default) lands on the rim / border; lower values pull labels inside the wedge (`65` ≈ mid-wedge); `>100` pushes them outside the pie. The cartesian polar analogue of `yOffset`.

dataLabelsConfig.positionRules.doc: Conditional overrides for the label's X/Y position offsets, evaluated against the same backing value as `textColorRules`. The first matching rule's offsets REPLACE `xOffset`/`yOffset` for that label; non-matching labels keep the base offsets.

dataLabelsConfig.ringLabelRadius.doc: Sunburst label placement — the label's distance ACROSS its ring as a PERCENT of the ring's radial thickness, measured from the inner edge.

dataLabelsConfig.sizeMin.doc: Min/max font size when a `size` field is mapped — the field's numeric range scales linearly across this px range.

dataLabelsConfig.textAngle.doc: Rotation in DEGREES applied to each label around its anchor point, same convention as the axes' `tickLabelAngle` (positive = clockwise, clamped to ±90 by the panel). Paint-time only: layout passes (overlap nudge, margin reservation) still measure the unrotated footprint.

dataLabelsConfig.textBackground.doc: When true, draw a filled rounded rect behind each label so the text reads cleanly over gridlines / dense marks instead of colliding with them.

dataLabelsConfig.textBackgroundBorderCol.doc: Border (stroke) color of the text-background rect. Unset = a neutral grey (`DEFAULT_BG_BORDER_COLOR`). Only drawn while `textBackgroundBorderWidth` is above 0.

dataLabelsConfig.textBackgroundBorderWid.doc: Border thickness (px) of the text-background rect. Unset / `0` = no border (the historical look, so no migration is needed).

dataLabelsConfig.textBackgroundColor.doc: Fill color of the text-background rect. `null` (the default) inherits the visualization's background color — white when that's transparent — so labels blend into the chart canvas while masking gridlines.

dataLabelsConfig.textBackgroundPadX.doc: Horizontal padding (px) added to EACH side of the text inside the background rect. Widens the rect left and right of the glyphs.

dataLabelsConfig.textBackgroundPadY.doc: Vertical padding (px) added to the top and bottom of the text inside the background rect.

dataLabelsConfig.textBackgroundRadius.doc: Corner radius (px) of the text-background rect. `0` = square corners.

dataLabelsConfig.textColorRules.doc: Conditional overrides for the label's text color, evaluated against the label's numeric value when it can be parsed as a number. The first matching rule's color wins; non-matching rules fall through to the standard color resolution chain (per-category override → hue scale → `color`).

dataLabelsConfig.underline.doc: Underlined label text. Optional for the same back-compat reason.

dataLabelsConfig.wrapMaxChars.doc: Target number of characters per line when `wrapText` is on. The wrapper aims for this width but breaks on the SPACE nearest the target — searching both directions — so lines land on word boundaries and never split mid-word (an over-long word simply overflows its line).

dataLabelsConfig.wrapText.doc: When true, long label text wraps onto multiple lines instead of rendering as a single run. The wrap point is chosen by `wrapMaxChars` (see below). SVG `<text>` has no auto-wrap, so the renderer pre-splits the string into `<tspan>` lines.

dataLabelsConfig.xOffset.doc: Pixel offset added to each label's x position after the chart scale lookup. Lets the user nudge labels relative to a bar end or a point — e.g. +12 to push them past the right edge of bars.

dataLabelsConfig.yOffset.doc: Pixel offset added to each label's y position.

dataLabelsEncodings.doc: Per-visual Data Labels encodings — which fields drive the label layer's x, y, hue, size, text. Optional for back-compat.

dataLabelsEncodings.geography.doc: Geo modes only — replaces the X/Y position rows on maps. The field whose values join to map regions; each label centers on its region's centroid.

dataLabelsEncodings.hue.doc: `measureSource` (tree layouts only — packed circles / treemap / sunburst): label color varies by a hierarchy-derived value instead of a dataset column — "rootGroup" (the node's outermost ancestor, categorical) or "depth" (nesting level, ordinal).

dataLabelsEncodings.r.doc: Retired: the R position row was dropped from the Data Labels shelf (pie labels sit at the wedge midpoint; the Distance nudge moves them radially, so a mapped field had nothing to drive). Kept optional so visuals saved with the slot load unchanged; nothing reads it.

dataLabelsEncodings.size.doc: Size supports only "depth" — root-group is categorical, and a font size needs an ordered value. Top level renders BIGGEST (sizeMax), the deepest level smallest (sizeMin); swap Min/Max to invert.

dataLabelsEncodings.value.doc: The label's text content. Single-field mode (`multiField` falsy): `field`'s row value is the label text. When `field` is unmapped, the label falls back to the `x` field's value (or `y`'s if x isn't mapped) so the user can scaffold position-only labels.

dataTableConfig.doc: Per-visual data table — an optional HTML table rendered under the chart (editor, in-app embed, published embed; image exports only when the Export modal's "Include data table" is checked).

dataTableConfig.caption.doc: Caption BELOW the table (a paragraph the table is described by). Null = no caption.

dataTableConfig.columnAlign.doc: Per-column alignment, keyed by the column's name (its header). An absent column takes its default — `defaultColumnAlign`.

dataTableConfig.firstColumnLikeOthers.doc: "Format first column like other columns". False = the first column's body cells take the `firstColumn*` font below.

dataTableConfig.headerBorderColor.doc: The rule under the header row.

dataTableConfig.hiddenPlottedColumns.doc: The "select" plotted table's unchecked columns ("sales (sum)", "Count", …), by header. A hide-list, so a column the chart starts computing later shows until unchecked. Unused by "all" (but kept, so switching back restores the picks) and by row tables.

dataTableConfig.maxRows.doc: Rows shown before a "Show all N rows" button. Null = every row (the box cleared); absent on intake = the default, 10.

dataTableConfig.numberAlign.doc: Legacy: the number-column alignment from before per-column choices. No control of its own any more; a stored value still serves as this visual's numbers & dates default. Null = the theme's.

dataTableConfig.plottedColumns.doc: "Columns" on an aggregating chart. Kept apart from `columns` so switching chart types doesn't flip the other picker.

dataTableConfig.selectedColumns.doc: The variables a "select" table shows, by (current) name. Unused by the other modes, but kept so switching back restores the picks.

dataTableConfig.showDownload.doc: A "Download CSV" link under the table.

dataTableConfig.title.doc: Title ABOVE the table — the HTML `<caption>`, so it is also the table's accessible name. Null = "Data for <visual title or name>".

fieldLevelOrderSpecs.doc: What the Fields panel's "Order by" picker was set to when each pinned order was computed, keyed by field name.

fieldLevelOrders.doc: Per-field user-pinned ordering of categorical / ordinal levels. Maps field name → ordered list of level values. The chart pipeline (aggregateStacks, makePositionScale) consults this when present and falls back to smart-sort otherwise.

fieldOrder.doc: The visual's column order (Fields panel / data tray drag), by name — applied last in the view chain, so it covers reshape and derived columns too. Optional: absent = the data set's own order.

labelsConfig.baseFont.text.legendFamily.doc: Optional legend-entry-label overrides (theme "Legend text" defaults). Each falls back to the shared field above, so legend labels follow the axis tick labels unless a theme splits them (resolveLegendTextFont).

labelsConfig.baseFont.titles.legendColor.doc: Optional legend section title color / size / style. Color + style fall back to the shared values; size falls back to `secondarySize`.

labelsConfig.baseFont.titles.prefixFamil.doc: Optional theme defaults for the chart-title PREFIX run (see `LabelsConfig.titlePrefix`). Each falls back to the RESOLVED chart title font at resolve time (`resolveTitlePrefixFont`), never to the shared fields directly, so the prefix tracks the title's own override.

labelsConfig.baseFont.titles.primaryAlig.doc: Theme-default alignments for the chart title / subtitle / legend section titles. These are the BASE the per-visual `titleAlignments` overrides layer on top of (see `titleAlignmentOf`) — kept out of `titleAlignments` itself so theme defaults don't read as user edits.

labelsConfig.baseFont.titles.secondaryCo.doc: Optional axis / facet title color + style, falling back to the shared `color` / `italic` / `underline` when unset.

labelsConfig.baseFont.titles.subtitleFam.doc: Optional per-slot families, falling back to the shared `family` like the weights above. `secondaryFamily` covers axis + facet titles.

labelsConfig.baseFont.titles.subtitleWei.doc: Optional per-slot weights. Each falls back to the shared `weight` (which doubles as the chart-title weight) when unset, so themes that only carry the single weight keep their look.

labelsConfig.facetTitleColorByValue.doc: "Color by facet": when true, each facet title is colored per facet VALUE via `facetTitleColors`. The stored colors stay put when this is off — unchecking reverts every title to its slot's resolved color without losing the picks, so re-checking restores them.

labelsConfig.facetTitleColors.doc: Sparse per-facet-value title colors, keyed by the facet VALUE string (a wrap panel key, or a grid row / column value). Missing entries fall back to the slot's resolved title color (the theme's title color unless a facet-title font override sets one).

labelsConfig.hiddenTitles.doc: "Titles shown" unchecks: a title slot set to `true` is not drawn and reserves no space, whatever text it holds. Sparse — showing a title deletes its entry, so absent = shown (the default). The typed text, font and offsets survive a hidden title, so re-checking restores it.

labelsConfig.legendTitles.doc: Legend title overrides, same three-state semantics as the axis titles: a missing entry falls back to the field / feature name; an entry set to `""` draws no legend header.

labelsConfig.titleAlignments.doc: Horizontal alignment per title slot. Missing entries fall back to "center" (the previous hard-coded default). Renderers consult this to place chart title / subtitle inside `width`, axis titles along the axis's spine, and legend titles inside the legend column.

labelsConfig.titleAngles.doc: Rotation per title slot, in degrees (-180…180, positive = clockwise), applied about the title's anchor point. Missing / 0 entries mean upright (the writes stay sparse — 0 is deleted).

labelsConfig.titleOffsets.doc: Per-title pixel offset applied AFTER the solver computes anchor positions. `+x` moves right, `+y` moves down (SVG convention). The solver also feeds these offsets into margin estimation so titles pushed outward grow the canvas reserve rather than clipping.

labelsConfig.titlePlacements.doc: Placement per title slot — only the per-panel facet-title slots (`facetTitle` for wrap panels, `facetPanelTitle` for compacted grids) consume it. Sparse: an entry is stored only for a side placement (`top` is deleted on write), so absent = the top band.

labelsConfig.titlePrefix.doc: Optional run of text drawn in front of the chart title — the "FIGURE 5." in "FIGURE 5. Distribution of …" — with its own font so it can be bold / colored / sized apart from the title proper.

labelsConfig.titleVerticalAlignments.doc: Vertical alignment per title slot. Missing entries fall back to "middle". Only the facet row-title strip consumes this today: it moves each row's title to the top / center / bottom of that row's plot rect, so rows of different heights line their titles up as chosen.

labelsConfig.xAxisTitle.doc: Axis title text as a THREE-STATE value: • `undefined` — never customized → renderers fall back to the field name (the sidebar shows that field name as a grayed placeholder). • `""` — user explicitly cleared it → NO title is drawn. • any other string — custom title.

labelsConfig.yAxisTitleHorizontal.doc: When true, the y-axis title is drawn upright (0°) instead of rotated -90°. Pairs with the auto-margin logic so a long horizontal title can push the plot rightward to fit.

legendConfig.doc: Per-visual legend layout (position, orientation, border, hidden channels). Optional for back-compat with visuals saved before this field existed — falls back to DEFAULT_LEGEND_CONFIG on load.

legendConfig.auxLegendSwatchColor.doc: Color used for length / angle / area / opacity legend swatches when they render as a STANDALONE section (no hue gradient to inherit from). `null` falls back to the historical `#4f8eda`.

legendConfig.auxLegendSwatchShape.doc: Glyph for Size-led legends (no Color in the section) — a `SHAPE_PALETTE` index. `null` = the marks' own shape. Shared across those sections like the aux swatch color / stroke above.

legendConfig.auxLegendSwatchStroke.doc: Border (stroke) color for the AREA (size) legend swatch circles. Only the area swatch is a filled shape with a meaningful outline — length / angle swatches are lines (their stroke IS the swatch color) and opacity swatches are borderless fills.

legendConfig.auxLegendSwatchStrokeWidth.doc: Outline width (px) for those Size glyphs. `null` = 1px.

legendConfig.backgroundColor.doc: Background color for the legend box. `null` means transparent — useful for inside legends that should let the chart show through.

legendConfig.borderColor.doc: Border-box stroke color. Only consulted when `showBorder` is true.

legendConfig.channels.doc: Per-quantitative-channel break + format overrides. Sparse: channels not present here fall back to `DEFAULT_LEGEND_CHANNEL_CONFIG`. The scale-building code reads `breaks` to override its domain; the legend renderer reads `format` + `breakCount` to lay out labels.

legendConfig.channels.angle.breakCount.doc: Number of break stops shown along the gradient / swatch list when `breaks` is empty. Ignored when `breaks` is non-empty (custom values override count). The legend's renderer may clamp this to a sensible minimum (typically 2).

legendConfig.channels.angle.breaks.doc: Explicit break values. When non-empty, defines BOTH the labels and the underlying scale's domain — the encoded mark color/size will span `[min(breaks), max(breaks)]` instead of the data's natural extent. Empty array = use `breakCount` with uniform interpolation across the data extent.

legendConfig.channels.angle.format.doc: d3-format spec applied to each break label. Empty string = use the legend's historical default (toFixed(2) for numeric, locale-date for temporal). Mirrors AxisConfig.customFormat from the axis tick UI so the user reuses the same mental model.

legendConfig.channels.area.breakCount.doc: Number of break stops shown along the gradient / swatch list when `breaks` is empty. Ignored when `breaks` is non-empty (custom values override count). The legend's renderer may clamp this to a sensible minimum (typically 2).

legendConfig.columnGap.doc: Horizontal gap, in pixels, between legend columns. Only meaningful when `columns > 1`. Defaults to 24.

legendConfig.columns.doc: How many columns the legend arranges its SECTIONS in — the sole control over that arrangement (`orientation` only governs how entries flow inside one section). `1` (default) always means a single column: the sections stack, whatever the position or orientation. With ≥2 legends mapped (e.g.

legendConfig.combineSameVariable.doc: When multiple encodings map to the SAME field, merge them into one legend section (a composed swatch + a single title) instead of drawing a separate legend per channel.

legendConfig.enabled.doc: Master toggle. When false, the legend doesn't render at all.

legendConfig.gradientBarBorderColor.doc: Border color. `null` / absent = the same neutral stone gray as the default tick color. Ignored while `gradientBarBorderWidth` is off.

legendConfig.gradientBarBorderWidth.doc: Border stroke thickness in pixels drawn around the gradient bar. `null` / absent / `0` = no border (the historical look). The border sits OUTSIDE the ramp — the bar grows by the border on every side — so the 0% / 100% stops, and the ticks / labels keyed to them, stay put when a border is turned on.

legendConfig.gradientBarLabelAlign.doc: How the gradient bar's break labels align. Horizontal bar: each label anchors its left edge / center / right edge at its break position. Vertical bar: text alignment within the label column beside the bar.

legendConfig.gradientBarLength.doc: Gradient bar length in pixels — the bar's height when the legend is vertical, its width when horizontal. `null` / absent = auto (the historical sizing: 8rem minimum height vertical, full legend width horizontal). Only consulted when `gradientLegendStyle` is `"bar"`.

legendConfig.gradientBarRadius.doc: Gradient bar corner radius in pixels. `null` / absent = 2 (the historical `rounded-sm` look); `0` = square corners.

legendConfig.gradientBarThickness.doc: Gradient bar thickness in pixels — the bar's width when the legend is vertical, its height when horizontal (the cross-axis of `gradientBarLength`). `null` / absent = 12 (the historical `w-3` / `h-3` strip).

legendConfig.gradientBarTickColor.doc: Tick color. `null` / absent = a neutral stone gray that reads on both light and dark legend backgrounds.

legendConfig.gradientBarTickLength.doc: Length in pixels of the tick marks drawn at each break stop, extending outward from the bar toward its labels. `null` / absent / `0` = no ticks (the historical look).

legendConfig.gradientBarTickThickness.doc: Tick stroke thickness in pixels. `null` / absent = 1. Ignored when `gradientBarTickLength` doesn't enable ticks.

legendConfig.gradientLegendStyle.doc: How a quantitative hue legend renders. `"bar"` (default) shows a single gradient strip with min / max labels — compact, classic scientific-paper look.

legendConfig.gradientLegendStyles.doc: The same bar / swatches choice for a continuous Saturation, Brightness or Opacity legend that stands alone (sharing a field with another channel forces swatches, as for Color). Absent = that legend's historical look (resolveRampLegendStyle). The bar draws with the shared gradient-bar settings below.

legendConfig.height.doc: Fixed height of the legend box in PIXELS (the px-truth behind the sidebar's "Legend height" input). `null` / absent = auto: the box hugs its content with the historical 4 px between entry rows.

legendConfig.heightUnit.doc: Display unit for the "Legend height" input. DISPLAY-ONLY, like `widthUnit`. Absent = px.

legendConfig.hidden.doc: Per-channel hide flags. A channel set to `true` is suppressed even when its encoding is mapped (handy for hiding redundant hue legends when hue and facet share a field).

legendConfig.hueLegendSwatchShape.doc: Shape drawn for each color (hue) legend swatch. `null` / undefined renders the historical rounded rectangle.

legendConfig.hueLegendSwatchSize.doc: Symbol radius (px) for hue legend swatches when `hueLegendSwatchShape` is set. `null` / undefined uses the default radius (5). Only affects shape swatches — the default rectangle ignores it.

legendConfig.insideX.doc: When `position === "inside"`, plot-area-normalized coordinates of the legend's top-left corner. (0, 0) is the bottom-left corner of the plot (where the two axis spines meet); (1, 1) is the top-right. Values may exceed [0, 1] to position the legend outside the plot rectangle.

legendConfig.orientation.doc: Layout direction within each section's swatch list — entries only. How the SECTIONS themselves are arranged is `columns`.

legendConfig.patternLegendBgColor.doc: Legend-swatch overrides for a PATTERN-led section that isn't paired with a hue color (standalone pattern legend).

legendConfig.shapeLegendFillColor.doc: Default fill color for shape legend swatches when the shape and hue encodings are different fields (so there's no single hue color to inherit). Per-category `shape.fillOverrides[value]` takes precedence when set; this just controls the otherwise-neutral fallback.

legendConfig.shapeLegendStrokeColor.doc: Companion stroke color for shape legend swatches. `null` falls back to the theme's `shape.outlineColor`. Useful when the shape legend's swatch color needs to read distinctly against the legend background.

legendConfig.shapeLegendStrokeWidth.doc: Outline width (px) for shape legend glyphs — standalone and in a combined (e.g. Color · Shape) section. `null` = the historical 1px.

legendConfig.showBorder.doc: Wrap the legend in a border box.

legendConfig.swatchOutlineColor.doc: Outline drawn around each COLOR swatch in the legend (hue / rug / combined color sections). Keeps pale swatches — e.g. the white midpoint of a diverging gradient — visible against the legend background.

legendConfig.swatchOutlineColors.doc: Per-section swatch outline color, keyed like `swatchShapes`. An entry wins over the legacy global `swatchOutlineColor` (which used to border every section at once); `null` = explicitly auto (pipe in the marks' outline color) even when the global is set.

legendConfig.swatchOutlineWidth.doc: Stroke width (px) for the swatch outline. `null` / absent / `0` = no outline (the historical look and the default — no separate on/off toggle, the width IS the switch).

legendConfig.swatchOutlineWidths.doc: Per-section swatch outline width (px), keyed like `swatchShapes`. Falls back to the legacy global `swatchOutlineWidth`, then the theme's default (`Theme.legendSwatchOutlineWidth`); `0` = no outline for that section (the width IS the switch), `null` = follow the theme.

legendConfig.swatchShapes.doc: Per-section swatch shape, keyed by the channel that LEADS the legend section (hue / outlineHue / saturation / brightness / pattern / opacity / rug). Lets each swatch-drawing legend use a distinct glyph so the user can tell them apart when several are mapped at once.

legendConfig.swatchSizes.doc: Per-section swatch radius (px), paired with `swatchShapes`. Absent = the theme's default (`Theme.legendSwatchSize`).

legendConfig.textAlign.doc: How each entry's label text aligns within its row. `null` / absent = the historical layout: the label cell hugs its text right beside the swatch, so there is nothing to align within.

legendConfig.textFont.doc: Per-visual styling for the legend ENTRY labels (the Legend panel's "Legend text" subsection). Sparse: every unset field falls through to the theme's legend-text defaults (`baseFont.text.legend*`, themselves falling back to the shared body-text font) — see `resolveLegendTextFont`.

legendConfig.width.doc: Fixed width of the legend box in PIXELS (the px-truth behind the sidebar's "Legend width" input, whatever unit it displays). `null` / absent = auto: the legend sizes itself to its content as it always has.

legendConfig.widthUnit.doc: Display unit for the "Legend width" input — px / in / cm at the CSS-standard 96 px/inch. DISPLAY-ONLY: `width` stays px. Absent = px.

mapConfig.doc: Per-visual map config (coordinate system, projection, geography level, focus region / custom viewport, no-data fill). Optional for back-compat with visuals saved before maps existed — falls back to DEFAULT_MAP_CONFIG on load. Without this the map state (e.g.

mapConfig.customViewport.doc: The viewport for `focusRegion: "custom"` — the box the user pans/zooms. Null until they switch to Custom (then it's seeded from the current view). Like a region, a custom viewport forces a world projection.

mapConfig.focusRegion.doc: Center + zoom the map on a continent/region. `"auto"` fits to the loaded geometry (legacy behavior). A specific region forces a world projection (albersUsa is US-only and would clip the rest of the globe). `"custom"` uses the user-dragged `customViewport`.

mapConfig.noDataPattern.doc: Optional pattern overlay for no-data regions: an index into `PATTERN_PALETTE` (lib/patterns), or null (default) for the solid `noDataFill`.

mapConfig.noDataPatternInk.doc: Ink color for `noDataPattern` (the pattern tiles' background is `noDataFill`). Inert while `noDataPattern` is null.

mapConfig.showBasemap.doc: When true (default), the geography region outlines draw as a backdrop behind the data marks (e.g. the Phase 3 bubble map). When false, the basemap is omitted and only the data marks render.

mapConfig.showNoDataRegions.doc: When true (default), every basemap feature draws — regions with no matching data row are painted with `noDataFill`, exactly like a matched row whose measure value is blank/NA. When false, only regions that join to a data row are drawn; the rest of the basemap is omitted.

tooltipConfig.doc: Per-visual tooltip config (enabled, visible fields, custom HTML/CSS). Same back-compat treatment as `legendConfig`.

tooltipConfig.customCss.doc: Optional CSS rules applied to a wrapping `<div class="vc-tooltip">`. Fully user-controlled — no sanitization, no fallback. Only applied while `useCustomHtml` is true (the sidebar hides the box otherwise).

tooltipConfig.customHtml.doc: Optional HTML template for tooltip content. When `useCustomHtml` is true, this template replaces the default field-list layout — `{{fieldName}}` placeholders are substituted with the hovered row's values (HTML-escaped to prevent injection).

tooltipConfig.hoverEnabled.doc: Master toggle for pointer-hover interactions (the "Show hover" checkbox under the Hover subsection). When off, the legend-highlight behavior below is disabled regardless of its own flag. Independent of `enabled`, which gates the mark tooltip.

tooltipConfig.hoverFade.doc: Fade the non-matched marks on hover. `undefined` → `true`.

tooltipConfig.hoverFadeAmount.doc: How strongly non-matched marks fade, 0–1 (0 = no change, 1 = fully transparent). Resulting opacity multiplier is `1 - hoverFadeAmount`. `undefined` → `0.85` (matched marks stay, others drop to ~15%).

tooltipConfig.hoverHighlightColor.doc: Recolor (fill) color applied to hovered marks when `hoverRecolor` is on. `undefined` → `DEFAULT_HOVER_HIGHLIGHT_COLOR`.

tooltipConfig.hoverOutlineColor.doc: Outline (stroke) color, independent of the recolor fill. `undefined` → `DEFAULT_HOVER_OUTLINE_COLOR`.

tooltipConfig.hoverOutlineWidth.doc: Outline stroke width in px when `hoverOutline` is on. `undefined` → `DEFAULT_HOVER_OUTLINE_WIDTH` (2).

tooltipConfig.hoverRecolor.doc: Repaint hovered marks' fill with `hoverHighlightColor` on hover — the opt-in "highlight with a color" toggle (reveals the color picker). `undefined` → `false`.

tooltipConfig.legendHighlight.doc: When true (and `hoverEnabled`), hovering a categorical legend entry highlights the matching marks per the appearance options below. Optional for back-compat — `undefined` is treated as `true`.

tooltipConfig.pointsOnly.doc: LINE CHARTS only (a connection field mapped on a scatter): restrict the full tooltip to the points that are actually DRAWN.

tooltipConfig.tooltipBackgroundColor.doc: Background fill. `null` = Auto: white in the light UI, dark stone in the dark UI. A set color also flips the text ink to whichever of black / white reads on it.

tooltipConfig.tooltipMaxWidth.doc: Tooltip box — the container every tooltip (default field list OR a custom HTML template) renders in. Every field here is SPARSE against the theme (Settings → Themes → Tooltips): an absent entry follows the theme live, a present one pins this visual. `resolveTooltipBox` is the one chain.

tooltipConfig.tooltipOutlineColor.doc: Outline (1px border) color. `null` = Auto: a light hairline in the light UI, a dark one in the dark UI.

tooltipConfig.tooltipShadowSize.doc: Drop-shadow size in px (the blur; the shadow also sits half that far below the box). `0` = no shadow.

tooltipConfig.useCustomHtml.doc: When true, the tooltip renders `customHtml` instead of the checkbox-driven field list. Enabling the toggle seeds empty HTML/CSS textareas with the defaults as a starter template. Optional for back-compat with visuals saved before this field existed — `undefined` is treated as `false`.

tooltipConfig.visibleFields.doc: Field names to show in the tooltip. Empty array = show every field present in the hovered row.
